This is related to #17762 .

Looking back it should've been obvious... since the static analyzer no longer sees the `import()` call, esbuild no longer resolves it in `--bundle` mode ([docs](https://esbuild.github.io/api/#bundle)), so the resulting source code looks like this:

```js
var obfuscated_import = (module_name) => import(
  /* @vite-ignore */
  module_name
);
```

There's obviously no error at build time, it just hits you at runtime when running the `.cjs` file because... well, esbuild is supposed to resolve the `import()`, but it's not, and a cjs only runtime has no idea what `import()` is.

I honestly don't know if this is fixable unless `node:crypto` is dropped, aka node 18 is dropped.

Another alternative would be to use a userland crypto package instead of something from the platform, but I don't know if that's doable or even worth it, this is getting ridiculous.

I'll come up with some patch-work on my end, I'll probably have to straight up remove that code from the bundle and cross my fingers.

body_text:
### Describe the problem

I got the idea of writing this issue after reading https://cpojer.net/posts/fastest-frontend-tooling. There’s no doubt that AI is a massive shift in code writing, and one of the most important ways to ensure that AI writes good code is by using the tools available; formatting, linting, type checking, building etc.

I love Svelte, i’ve used it every day at work since Svelte 3. IMO, Svelte is the perfect FE framework for AI because of how little code is necessary to achieve what you want, and there’s usually only «one way» to do things. The syntax is easy to understand, and it’s difficult to do things wrong. However, I have started to feel certain pain points when developing Svelte with AI when it comes to the feedback loop of the tools available. I’ve added optimizations like only formatting changed files in a branch, only running lint on changed files (which works in most cases), and telling it to use svelte-check only at the latest step.

However, it still feels like there’s a way to go. Tools like svelte-fast-check (really cool, but has some bugs that makes it not usable atm), Rolldown, Biome and the OX tool suite seem like great advancements. However, to me it doesn’t seem like the OX team (are able to?) prioritize Svelte when developing their tools. You can format and lint in the script-tags, but that isn’t enough to be usable IMO. Biome has experimental support, but it’s experimental. And OX seems to maybe be the most likely tool to use with Vite considering they’re from the same company.

I may be wrong here, and i most likely are, but i feel like i haven’t found any signs that performance (down to the millisecond/seconds scale) is going to be prioritized in the near future.

So therefore i’m asking the question: What’s the roadmap for making Svelte building, bundling, linting, formatting etc. as fast as the other alternatives? Large React applications can now be built, linted and formatted in seconds, but Svelte is still on the performance of pre-rust tooling upgrades.

### Describe the proposed solution

I’m not sure what the best solution to this problem is, but it feels like this is something that will become more important now that the feedback loop is moving away from the VSCode interface via plugins for humans to read, and moving towards the CLI for machines to read.

I know that tools like Cursor give access to the language server in their AI-panels, but for many workflows using Cursor is not the best option anymore.

### Importance

### Describe the problem

https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/345b8ed69f0b74b91d7ede4052e302c85e3f9cd1/packages/svelte/types/index.d.ts#L3221-L3222
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/345b8ed69f0b74b91d7ede4052e302c85e3f9cd1/packages/svelte/types/index.d.ts#L3307
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/345b8ed69f0b74b91d7ede4052e302c85e3f9cd1/packages/svelte/types/index.d.ts#L3331-L3332


Currently, `$state` and its variants has two definitions, one that takes a generic initial T, and one where we don't pass an initial value at all (implicit `undefined`).

When annotating reactive `$state` with a union type containing null:
```svelte.ts
let numThingOrNull : number | null = $state(null); // number | null
```
TypeScript claims `numThingOrNull` is `number | null`, but control flow checking later actually type-narrows to _only_ `null`:
```ts
numThingOrNull?.toFixed(); // Property 'toFixed' does not exist on type 'never'.
```
As far as it's concerned, we have not reassigned to `numThingOrNull` in between, so it could only ever be `null`. However, this becomes a type issue when e.g. we want to use `$derived`:
```svelte.ts
let numAsStringOrUndef = $derived(numThingOrNull?.toFixed());
// Property 'toFixed' does not exist on type 'never'.
```
As, again, as far as TS is concerned, this is just a function that is being run one time. It has no concept of `$derived` re-running in response to `numThingOrNull` being reassigned later in the code or in a separate function.

The same for if guards:
```ts
if (numThingOrNull) {
	console.log(numThingOrNull?.toFixed());
	// Property 'toFixed' does not exist on type 'never'.
}
```
Which impacts e.g. use in `$effect`.

This also illustrates the larger divergence from TS and the core of the issue:
```svelte.ts
let plainNull = null; // any - it's common to want to reassign over null

// but in Svelte...
let willBeThing = $state(null); // null
```

## Existing Workarounds

A workaround exists by instead moving the type to the function generic:
```svelte.ts
let numThingOrNull = $state<number | null>(null); // number | null
numThingOrNull?.toFixed();
```
This lets TS know that the "function output" of `$state` could be either `number` or `null`.
However, it is not immediately clear to the user why this syntax works and the `let varName : Type` form does not, even if it makes sense when presented this way.

You could also explicitly cast:
```svelte.ts
let numThingOrNull = $state(null) as number | null;
numThingOrNull?.toFixed();
```
But that is usually a recommendation of last resort.

### Describe the proposed solution

Prepend non-generic overloads for `null` before the existing generic overloads, for `$state`, `$state.raw`, and `$state.eager`

```d.ts
declare function $state(initial: null): any;
declare function $state<T>(initial: T): T;
declare function $state<T>(): T | undefined;
```

```d.ts
export function raw(initial: null): any;
export function raw<T>(initial: T): T;
export function raw<T>(): T | undefined;
```

```d.ts
export function eager(initial: null): any;
export function eager<T>(value: T): T;
// tangent: is it deliberate that eager doesn't have the T | undefined one?
```

Returning `any` makes the return type transparent to the variable annotation, so control flow narrowing operates on the annotation as expected.
```svelte.ts
let thing = $state(null); // any
let numExplicit : number | null = $state(null); // number | null
numExplicit?.toFixed(); // works fine, type checker doesn't complain
```
This matches how vanilla TS handles `null` literals.

Note that the order of declaration matters. If you have it _after_ the generic:
```d.ts
declare function $state<T>(initial: T): T;
declare function $state<T>(): T | undefined;
declare function $state(initial: null): any;
```
`declare function $state<T>(initial: T): T;` will take precedence and the type checker will stop there.

Note that the definition where we pass initial null is explicitly non-generic. If we instead tried:
```d.ts
declare function $state<T>(initial: null): any;
```
This would unintentionally widen when the existing workaround is used:
```svelte.ts
let thing = $state<Thing | null>(null); // any, instead of the declared Thing | null
```
We can let the existing declaration take over for such cases.

We deliberately omit new type declaration for `$state.snapshot` because it transforms reactive state to a POJO, so TypeScript's usual type/flow checking model is already accurate.

### Importance

### Describe the bug

When awaiting a Promise.all inside a $derived I can see the await_waterfall warning. I'm possibly misunderstanding the warning but I don't think it should warn about it.
The warning can be seen in the REPL console upon first load.

In my project I was also getting await_reactivity_loss from the same code that produced this warning which actually had an impact on the app. I haven't been able to reproduce that in a REPL but they're possibly related

https://svelte.dev/playground/7150c39aa545498bba86de0a18506707?version=5.55.1

body_text: ### Summary Hi! While working with Svelte 5 in an SPA setup, we noticed **detached DOM nodes accumulating over time** after components are destroyed. In our case, repeatedly mounting/unmounting a component like: ```svelte {#if chatId} {/if} ``` eventually leads to a noticeable number of detached elements (e.g. `HTMLVideoElement`, wrappers, buttons) remaining in memory. After several open/close cycles, this can grow quite large. In heap snapshots, these nodes appear with `detachedness != 0`, often retained via `system / Context` (closure scope). This seems consistent with the behavior described in Chrome DevTools documentation: [https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/memory-problems/heap-snapshots#uncover_dom_leaks](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/memory-problems/heap-snapshots#uncover_dom_leaks) — where a reference to a single node can keep the whole detached subtree alive. --- ### What might be happening From what we can see, Svelte correctly removes nodes from the document (`node.remove()`) and clears effect internals. However, the **detached subtree itself remains internally connected** (via parent/child relationships). If any closure still references one of those nodes (for example via `bind:`, event handlers, or template locals), the entire subtree may remain reachable. Since compiled templates keep multiple DOM references within a shared closure, it’s not straightforward to fully clean this up at the application level. --- ### Reproduction Repo: [https://github.com/dimensi/svelte-dom-leak-repro](https://github.com/dimensi/svelte-dom-leak-repro) * SvelteKit SPA (`ssr = false`) * Run: `npm install && npm run dev` **Steps:** 1. Take heap snapshot (A) 2. Interact with rows (play/pause, counters) 3. Click **“Stress 600 remounts”** 4. Click garbage collect in devtoos 5. Take snapshot (B) Detached DOM nodes tend to increase, especially after interactions. --- ### Possible direction (just for discussion) One idea could be to extend teardown so that detached subtrees are not only removed from the document, but also **fully disconnected internally**, for example: * Clearing delegated event handler storage (`event_symbol`) * Resetting media elements (`video/audio`) * Recursively removing children to break parent/child chains This might help avoid situations where a single lingering reference retains the entire subtree. --- ### Experimental patch (PoC) This is just a proof of concept that helped in our case (significantly reduced detached nodes), not necessarily a suggested final solution: ```js export function remove_effect_dom(node, end) { while (node !== null) { var next = node === end ? null : get_next_sibling(node); node.remove(); deep_cleanup_node(node); node = next; } } function deep_cleanup_node(node) { while (node.firstChild) { deep_cleanup_node(node.firstChild); node.firstChild.remove(); } } ``` --- ### Environment * Svelte 5.x (observed on 5.55.x) * Chrome DevTools heap snapshots

### Describe the bug When using a reactive remote function, for example: ```js const data = $derived(await getData(days)); ``` and trigger a change (`days`) will cause the browser to freeze/lockup. This same code works if you switch to client-side synchronous data, for example: ```js const data = $derived(generate(days)); ``` This was first reported as a LayerChart [issue](https://github.com/techniq/layerchart/issues/895) but I'm unable to find any cause and looks like a potential svelte async scheduling issue. ### Reproduction [repo](https://github.com/techniq/layerchart-async-repro) (notable this [route](https://github.com/techniq/layerchart-async-repro/blob/main/src/routes/remote/%2Bpage.svelte)) ```svelte

body_text:
## Describe the bug

Since 5.25, deriveds declared with `let` can be reassigned; the docs describe the lifetime as

> Derived expressions are recalculated when their dependencies change, but you can temporarily override their values by reassigning them

For a `.svelte.ts` module compiled with **client** codegen this holds in every context I measured (owned and unowned, flat and chained). Under **server** codegen the documented lifetime does not exist: after the reassignment the derived is never evaluated again, so the override survives every dependency change, permanently.

```ts
// store.svelte.ts — universal code, runs during SSR and on the client
let seed = $state(1);
let d = $derived.by(() => seed * 10);

d;          // 10
d = 999;    // override
seed = 2;   // dependency change
d;          // client build: 20 (documented) · server build: 999, forever
```

That means a shared rune store (the "universal reactivity" use case) has two different override semantics depending on which build executes it — e.g. an optimistic-UI override applied during SSR is never corrected server-side — and nothing in the docs mentions a difference.

The practical sharp edge is that test setups fall into the server world unnoticed. With Vitest, `environment: 'node'` gives you the SSR transform (server codegen). And the jsdom default without `resolve.conditions: ['browser']` produces a third, mixed state: client codegen but the *server* top-level `svelte` entry, where override semantics are client-like but `flushSync` is a silent no-op and `$effect.root` effects never fire. We first noticed all this as the same test sequence yielding contradictory results in two files of one repo.

Related, but not the same: #15934 / #15414 cover unowned per-read re-evaluation in the client build — that behaviour does not break the documented override lifetime; the server-codegen divergence reported here is a separate, undocumented one.

**Question:** is the server behaviour intended (i.e. override lifetime is only specified for the client build)? If so, could the docs state that overrides are permanent under SSR/server codegen — and should reassigning a derived in server code perhaps warn in DEV?

## Reproduction

Repository-free repro (a REPL cannot show this — the playground always runs mounted client code, which is exactly the one world that matches the docs):

https://github.com/urbicon/svelte-derived-override-server-codegen — a minimal vitest project with three projects (node env → server codegen; jsdom default → client codegen + server entry; jsdom with `resolve.conditions: ['browser']` → full client). `bun install && bunx vitest run` prints the matrix; the README carries the full result table and the ~20-line scenario module.

| context | codegen | override after dependency change | derived eval count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| node env, flat | server | **999 — survives forever** | 1 (never re-evaluated after override) |
| node env, chained | server | **survives** (through the chain) | inner 1 / outer 4 |
| jsdom default, flat/chained/owned | client (+ server entry) | 20 / 21 — documented | 2 |
| jsdom + browser condition, flat/chained/owned | client | 20 / 21 — documented | 2 |

## Logs

No errors or warnings are emitted in any of the cases — the divergence is silent.

## System Info

- svelte 5.56.10, @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte 7.3.0, vitest 4.1.11, jsdom 30.0.1
- macOS (darwin arm64), node v25.2.1

## Severity

### Describe the bug

I am referring to my previous issue #18491, which was closed by #18518. The problem is still there in the latest version (5.57.0). I tried to follow the explanation of the PR and played with adding `source` and `file` in various forms and I couldn't get it working. I tried to inspect the variables in `node_modules/svelte/src/compiler/utils/mapped_code.js` inside the function `combine_sourcemaps` and checking conditions, reversing orders, etc. but I couldn't find the root cause.

### Reproduction

Since the reproduction can't work in the REPL, and since it is fairly small, I'll provide the files here.

Start from the svelte template in `npm create vite@latest`, install `magic-string`, and edit only these two files:

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { svelte } from '@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte'
import MagicString from 'magic-string'

// https://vite.dev/config/
export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [
        {
            name: "tst",
            transform(code, id) {
                if (!id.includes('App.svelte')) {
                    return
                }
                const m = new MagicString(code)
                m.appendRight(10, 'let leben = 42\n\n')
                return {
                    code: m.toString(),
                    map: m.generateMap(/* add {file: id}, {source: id}, {file: 'App.svelte'}, etc */),
                }
            },
        },
        svelte()
    ],
})

## Description

When working with large lists (1000+ items) in SvelteKit, hydration can be noticeably slow compared to the initial SSR render. This affects Time to Interactive (TTI) metrics significantly.

## Reproduction

Rendering a list of 2000 items with dynamic content shows a 300-500ms hydration delay on mid-range devices.

## Suggestion

Consider implementing virtual hydration or lazy hydration strategies:
1. Only hydrate visible items initially
2. Defer hydration of off-screen items until they enter the viewport
3. Provide a `lazy` directive for components that can be hydrated later

This would significantly improve TTI for content-heavy pages like e-commerce listings or social feeds.

### Describe the bug A component-owned `$derived` remains reachable after `unmount()` when its last reader is hidden, a nested reactive object is replaced while hidden, and the reader is shown again. This reproduces on **Svelte 5.57.0** using only public Svelte APIs. It does not require SvelteKit, Vite, HMR, browser extensions, exceptions, or imports from `svelte/internal`. **AI disclosure:** This report and minimal reproduction were prepared by OpenAI Codex (AI) at my request. The tests described below were actually executed locally. We hope the concrete reproduction and control cases are still helpful to the Svelte maintainers. ### Reproduction [Complete runnable reproduction and raw results](https://gist.github.com/kmplngj/22ab718261121f8afebe0a9750ff3672). ```sh git clone https://gist.github.com/22ab718261121f8afebe0a9750ff3672.git svelte-reconnect-repro cd svelte-reconnect-repro npm install --ignore-scripts npm test -- replace ``` The two application files are: **shared.svelte.js** ```js export const shared = $state({ visible: true, data: { value: 0 }, locale: 'en' }); ``` **Retained.svelte** ```svelte
{#if shared.visible} {label} {:else} Loading {/if}
``` The runner compiles these files using `svelte/compiler` with `dev: false` and `hmr: false`. For each of 30 component instances it: 1. Creates a plain `marker` object, passes it as a prop, and retains only a `WeakRef` to it outside the cycle. 2. Mounts the component and calls `flushSync()`. 3. Sets `shared.visible = false` and flushes. 4. Replaces `shared.data = { value: id }` and flushes. 5. Sets `shared.visible = true` and flushes. 6. Awaits `unmount(instance)`. After all cycles it crosses task boundaries and forces GC ten times. The marker references are checked only afterward. **Expected:** All 30 markers are collectible after unmount. **Actual:** All 30 survive, although the document contains zero element children. The runner intentionally exits with code 1 when markers remain. ### Logs and controls Five separate processes per mode, 30 instances per process: | Mode | Operation while reader is hidden | Retained markers in the five runs | | --- | --- | --- | | `replace` | Replace nested object | 30, 30, 30, 30, 30 | | `mount-only` | No hide/show or data change | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 | | `toggle` | Hide/show without changing data | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 | | `mutate` | Mutate `shared.data.value` in place | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 | ```json {"svelte":"5.57.0","mode":"replace","cycles":30,"retained":30,"remainingElements":0} ``` Run the controls with `npm test -- mount-only`, `npm test -- toggle`, and `npm test -- mutate`. Each exits successfully. ### Suspected runtime cause The retaining path appears to be a long-lived source's `reactions` array → orphan derived → component closure/props. In `get()`, a previously evaluated, disconnected derived is marked `CONNECTED` before `update_derived()`. If the dependency list changes, `update_dependencies()` already adds it to dependencies' `reactions` arrays. The subsequent `reconnect()` adds it again. Later `remove_reaction()` removes only one occurrence, leaving an entry even though the derived has no remaining readers. As a diagnostic experiment only, preventing duplicate insertion in `reconnect()` changed the public-API reproduction from 30 retained markers to 0. The published reproduction uses the **unmodified** release. I am not proposing that this guard is necessarily the correct or complete production fix. Related: #18623 and its open PR #18709 also concern retention after unmount, but that proposed change targets `last_scheduled_effect`. This example needs nested dependency replacement and points to `source.reactions` instead; please consolidate if the maintainers consider it the same underlying issue. The exception-cleanup fix #18703 shipped in 5.57.0 does not eliminate this reproduction. ### System Info - Svelte: 5.57.0, exact package version in the reproduction - Node.js: 26.8.1 - jsdom: 30.0.1 - OS: macOS 26.6.2, arm64 - Compiler: client output, `dev: false`, `hmr: false` - Node flags: `--expose-gc --conditions=browser` ### Severity annoyance — repeated refresh/navigation cycles can accumulate state from unmounted components in a long-running application.

### Describe the bug With async mode on and SvelteKit's `forkPreloads` enabled, **hovering** a link — not clicking it — throws and replaces the current page with Kit's 500 error page: ``` TypeError: Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string at to_class at Module.set_class at .../child.svelte:22:6 at update_reaction at update_effect at flush_queued_effects at Batch.flush ``` The value is `Symbol(uninitialized)` — Svelte's own `UNINITIALIZED`. The speculative forked render reads a derived belonging to the other batch before it has been evaluated, gets the sentinel back, and hands it to the DOM writers; `to_class()` then does `'' + value`. `runtime.js` already documents the precondition: > In a fork it's possible that a derived is executed and gets reactions, then commits, but is never re-executed. This is possible when the derived is only executed once in the context of a new branch which happens before `fork.commit()` runs. In this case, the derived still has `UNINITIALIZED` as its value […] That handling keeps the derived DIRTY so it re-executes on read, but the attribute writers read the raw `.v` first. `class` is where it fails loudly. Other attributes take the same sentinel through `set_attribute()` and would stringify it just as readily, or render something wrong without throwing. ### Reproduction No REPL: `forkPreloads` is a SvelteKit option and the fork is driven by the router's hover-preload, so this needs an app. Stock SvelteKit, no other dependencies. Verified on a cold dev server, 5/5. ```js // vite.config.js import { sveltekit } from "@sveltejs/kit/vite"; export default { plugins: [ sveltekit({ compilerOptions: { experimental: { async: true } }, experimental: { forkPreloads: true, remoteFunctions: true }, }), ], }; ``` ```html
%sveltekit.body%
``` ```svelte hover me ``` ```js // src/routes/repro/thing.remote.js import { query } from "$app/server"; export const getThing = query(async () => { await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400)); return { id: "x" }; }); ``` ```svelte ``` ```svelte ``` Load `/repro`, hover the link, don't click. Three variants, each as its own route with everything on disk before a cold start, 3 runs each — all clean, so each of these looks load-bearing: - `class={props.label}` instead of `class={klass(props.label)}`. A call compiles to a derived; a bare reference is inlined. - `await new Promise(...)` instead of `await getThing()`. - dropping `disabled={accepted === thing.id}`, so no second prop reads the awaited value. ### Logs ```shell ``` ### System Info ```shell ### System Info `svelte@5.57.0`, `@sveltejs/kit@3.0.0-next.27`, `vite@8.3.0`, Chromium, Linux, dev mode. ``` ### Severity Blocks using `forkPreloads`. Anything computing a class through a helper is exposed, which is every shadcn-svelte component via `cn()`. Returning early from `set_class`, `set_attribute` and `set_attributes` when the value is `UNINITIALIZED` stops the throw and makes hover-preloading work, but it only suppresses the symptom — it doesn't stop the fork reading a derived before it's evaluated.

### Describe the bug Synchronous throw errors out as cryptic `null.f` access instead of the original error in production. ### Reproduction ```svelte

{await load()}

{#snippet pending()}

pending

{/snippet} {#snippet failed(error)}

{error.message}

{/snippet} ``` compile with ```js { generate: "client", dev: false, experimental: { async: true } } ``` Mount it, wait for `ready`, and click `invalidate`. - Expected: the boundary renders `original error`. - Actual: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'f')` escapes the boundary, which keeps displaying `ready`. - The same problem occurs if the initial promise is still pending. - The example deliberately throws a normal `Error`; no application code accesses a property of `null` or `undefined`. This will NOT manifest in svelte playground because the playground uses `dev: true`. ### Logs ```shell ``` ### System Info ```shell N/A ``` ### Severity annoyance

### Describe the bug `schedule_effect` casts away a null that `Batch.#process` sets deliberately: ```js // src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js export function schedule_effect(effect) { /** @type {Batch} */ (current_batch).schedule(effect); } ``` `#process()` nulls `current_batch` before it flushes effects, and only repopulates it on the legacy-updates path: ```js // any writes should take effect in a subsequent batch current_batch = null; if (updates.length > 0) { var batch = Batch.ensure(); … } … flush_queued_effects(render_effects); flush_queued_effects(effects); ``` If an effect flushed there reaches the self-invalidation block in `update_reaction`, it calls `schedule_effect` against that null and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule')`. Three conditions have to line up: 1. **The effect runs inside `Batch.#process` → `flush_queued_effects`.** In the reproduction the child is mounted by a state change, so its first run happens during the microtask batch flush rather than at mount. 2. **The effect writes a source in the same run in which that source first becomes one of its dependencies.** `update_dependencies` attaches the reaction to `source.reactions` only *after* `fn()` returns, so at write time `mark_reactions` cannot mark the effect dirty. It stays `CLEAN` and the source lands in `untracked_writes` — the `$effect(() => x++)` case described in the comment in `sources.js`. 3. **`flushSync()` runs after that write, within the same effect run.** The write itself calls `Batch.ensure()`, which repopulates `current_batch`; `flushSync`'s `finally` then nulls it again. `update_reaction` then reaches: ```js if ( is_runes() && untracked_writes !== null && !untracking && deps !== null && (reaction.f & (DERIVED | MAYBE_DIRTY | DIRTY)) === 0 ) { for (…) schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation(untracked_writes[i], reaction); } ``` The effect is `CLEAN` (condition 2) and is by now in `source.reactions` (attached by `update_dependencies` just above), so `schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation` matches `effect === reaction` and calls `schedule_effect`. Removing any single condition avoids the throw, verified individually: - Drop the `flushSync()` call. - Read `x` unconditionally so it is an established dependency before the run that writes it. `mark_reactions` then marks the effect `DIRTY` and the `(reaction.f & (DERIVED | MAYBE_DIRTY | DIRTY)) === 0` guard fails. - Mount the child directly instead of revealing it via a state change, so its first run no longer happens inside `#process`. ### Affected versions | version | result | | --- | --- | | 5.53.0 | works | | 5.54.0 | **throws** | | 5.57.1 | **throws** | Introduced by #17805 (*chore: refactor scheduling*, merged 2026-03-08), which moved scheduling from the module-global `queued_root_effects` array onto `current_batch`. Before that, `schedule_effect` never touched `current_batch`. The function is unchanged on `main` as of today. We hit this in production on a SvelteKit app: ~120 events over 7 days, across several releases, Chrome 152/153. Independently hit by another app on 5.56 with the same diagnosis: intent-hq/cloudlands-fe#2547. ### Related, but not duplicates Several open issues look like the same underlying invariant at different call sites: #18522 (`batch.transfer_effects` null after a top-level `flushSync`), #18799 (`batch.increment` null during async component init), and #18546 (scheduling bails after a batch is dropped). #18758's `flushSync` guard does not cover this one, since it fires only for a `BRANCH_EFFECT`/`ROOT_EFFECT` mid-update, and here `flushSync` is called inside a plain user `$effect`. ### On a PR Happy to open one. `Batch.ensure().schedule(effect)` fixes the reproduction and leaves the effect tree reactive afterwards (I checked specifically, given #18546 describes a failure mode where the root goes permanently non-reactive). But since the four issues above may share a cause, you may prefer a single fix upstream of all of them rather than a guard at this call site. Say which direction you want and I'll put it together with a test. ### Reproduction https://github.com/ndri/svelte-repro-batch-schedule `pnpm install && pnpm dev`, then click **Mount the child**. The child renders (`x = 1`) and an uncaught `TypeError` is reported on the page and in the console. The essential part is two files: ```svelte {#if show}{/if} ``` ```svelte

x = {x}

``` Note the throw happens in the microtask that flushes the batch, so it does **not** propagate out of the click handler and a `try`/`catch` there will not catch it. The reproduction listens on `window.onerror` to display it. ### Logs ```shell TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule') in $effect in Child.svelte in App.svelte Production build, symbolicated, from 5.57.0: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule') at schedule_effect (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:1240:39) at schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation (svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:220:4) at update_reaction (svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:274:5) at update_effect (svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:490:18) at flush_queued_effects (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:1100:4) at Batch.#process (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:389:3) at Batch.flush (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:619:9) at svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:866:13 at run_all (svelte/src/internal/shared/utils.js:47:9) at svelte/src/internal/client/dom/task.js:10:2 ``` ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 26.7 CPU: (12) arm64 Apple M2 Max Memory: 96.53 MB / 32.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 24.11.1 npm: 11.6.0 pnpm: 10.15.0 bun: 1.3.7 Browsers: Chrome: 153.0.8010.50 Firefox: 156.0 Safari: 27.0 npmPackages: svelte: 5.57.1 => 5.57.1 ``` ### Severity annoyance

### Describe the bug **Title:** `invariant_violation: "Batch has scheduled effects"` when a pending async batch is rebased twice (5.57.1, `experimental.async`) ### Describe the bug With `experimental.async`, a batch that is waiting on an `await` gets rebased whenever another batch commits. If the rebase re-runs an `{#each}` block and an item value changes, the each block calls `internal_set(item.v, …)`. That schedules the item's effects onto the pending batch. The rebase in `Batch.#commit` traverses only once: ```js // reactivity/batch.js (5.57.1), inside #commit if (batch.#scheduled.length > 0 && !batch.#decrement_queued) { batch.apply(); for (var root of batch.#resolve()) { batch.#traverse(root, [], []); } } ``` The effects scheduled during that traversal are left in the pending batch's `#scheduled`. `#process` handles this case with a `while (this.#scheduled.length > 0)` loop; this path doesn't. The next unrelated commit rebases the pending batch again and hits the DEV check added in #18508: ```js if (DEV && !batch.#decrement_queued) { invariant(batch.#scheduled.length === 0, 'Batch has scheduled effects'); } ``` In production the leftover effects never run, so the DOM stays stale. Adding a drain loop around the traversal above silences the invariant, but the DOM is still stale. I think that's because `#traverse(root, [], [])` throws away the render effects it collects. So I haven't included a proposed fix. Behaviour of the reproduction below: | Version | Mode | Error | Final render (expected `item 1`) | |---|---|---|---| | 5.57.0 | dev | none | `item 0` (stale) | | 5.57.1 | dev | `invariant_violation: "Batch has scheduled effects"` | `item 1` | | 5.57.1 | prod (`vite build` + `vite preview`) | none | `item 0` (stale) | So the stale render already happened in 5.57.0; #18508's new invariant is what surfaces it. In our real app the invariant is thrown from the microtask flush on every following commit. A superforms store update via `createSubscriber` commits again straight away, which gives about 2,500 errors/s. The tab freezes and the heap grows about 20–50 MB/s until the tab is killed. This only happens in dev builds, so we've pinned 5.57.0 for now. ### Reproduction ### Reproduction A minimal Vite project. The Svelte playground isn't used because the bug needs `experimental.async` and a dev build. `package.json` ```json { "type": "module", "scripts": { "dev": "vite", "build": "vite build", "preview": "vite preview" }, "devDependencies": { "@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte": "7.3.1", "svelte": "5.57.1", "vite": "8.3.1" } } ``` `svelte.config.js` ```js export default { compilerOptions: { experimental: { async: true } } }; ``` `vite.config.js` ```js import { svelte } from '@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte'; import { defineConfig } from 'vite'; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [svelte()] }); ``` `index.html` ```html
``` `src/main.js` ```js import { mount } from 'svelte'; import App from './App.svelte'; mount(App, { target: document.getElementById('app') }); ``` `src/App.svelte` ```svelte {#each items as n}

item {n}

{/each}

c {c}

slow {await slow(a)}

``` Steps: 1. `npm install && npm run dev`, then open the page and wait for `slow 0`. 2. Click **a**, then **b**, then **c**, all within one second (before `slow(a)` resolves). What happens, batch by batch: - Click **a** starts batch A, which is pending on `await slow(a)`. - Click **b** starts batch B, which commits and rebases A. `a * b` goes from 0 to 1 in A's view, so the each block updates `item.v`, and the `

item {n}

` effect is scheduled onto A. Nothing drains it. - `a * b` is used so that in B's own view (`a = 0`) the item value stays 0. That keeps `item.v` out of B, which would otherwise make B merge into A instead of rebasing it. - Click **c** starts batch C, an unrelated change that commits and rebases A again. The invariant fires. **Expected:** no error, and the page ends with `item 1`, `c 1`, `slow 1`. **Actual (dev):** `invariant_violation` as above. **Actual (prod):** no error, but the page shows `item 0`. The steps use fast clicks; the invariant fired every time in headless Chromium using Playwright's `click()` with no delays. ### Logs ``` Svelte error: invariant_violation An invariant violation occurred, meaning Svelte's internal assumptions were flawed. This is a bug in Svelte, not your app — please open an issue at https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte, citing the following message: "Batch has scheduled effects" https://svelte.dev/e/invariant_violation at invariant_violation (svelte/src/internal/client/errors.js) at invariant (svelte/src/internal/shared/dev.js) at #commit (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js) at #process (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js) at Batch.flush (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js) at run_all / run_micro_tasks (svelte/src/internal/client/dom/task.js) ``` This is the stack that scheduled the leftover effect, captured in our app with a temporary hook in `Batch#schedule`: ``` Batch.schedule → schedule_effect → mark_reactions → internal_set → each.js block effect (`if (item.v) internal_set(item.v, value)`) → update_effect → #traverse → #commit (rebase of the pending batch) → #process → Batch.flush → run_micro_tasks ``` ### Logs ```shell ``` ### System Info ```shell svelte 5.57.1 (also present on main as of 2026-09-30) @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte 7.3.1, vite 8.3.1 Node 24.8.0, Windows 11 Chromium (Playwright 1.63) and Chrome (our Electron-based desktop app) ``` ### Severity blocking an upgrade

Enabling strict Svelte Twoslash tooltips for [Svelte documentation tooltip tracking issue](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte.dev/issues/649) rejects **237 of 489 fenced Svelte snippet instances** in this repository's synced documentation (59 Markdown files). The complete failing-block inventory is below. ### What needs updating Give partial examples hidden setup, companion-file context, or appropriate types. Handle intentional type/compiler errors explicitly without changing their teaching intent or suppressing diagnostics globally. Update original sources, not generated site copies. These are **integration compatibility failures**, not a claim that every example is intrinsically wrong.
Audit method, versions, and source locations - Extracted actual `svelte` code tokens using the site's Markdown tokenizer, then checked each through `render_content`. Fences appearing as literal text inside Markdown examples are excluded. - Versions: `@twinkleplop/twoslash-svelte@0.2.1`, `svelte@5.56.4`, `svelte2tsx@0.7.56`, adapter TypeScript `5.9.3`. Strict diagnostics; the site's ambient Svelte/Kit/environment and synthetic route declarations are included. - Each snippet is checked independently. Diagnostics come from its first failing JS/TS variant; missing surrounding context can account for failures. - Upstream source links are pinned to `020242d6bef059df9ae8c13dc8dbff4c9b31e0ff` and matched to the exact snippets, including message/type sources behind generated documentation. - Each block distinguishes upstream and synced-page lines. Fence numbers count only actual Svelte code tokens within the synced page. - Identical diagnostics within a block are deduplicated. Generated `index.tsx` offsets are omitted; compiler/parser error codes are included.
### Failing blocks
Show all 237 failing blocks, grouped by source file Key: **L** = upstream opening-fence line; **F** = actual Svelte fence number in the synced page; **site L** = synced-page line. Expand the diagnostic catalog below for the linked error messages.

### Describe the bug

Hi, human here, below I will post the AI findings I had (Idk what the AI policy of this repo is, so if its forbidden feel free to just close this. But basically I saw a tweet here https://x.com/nullvoxpopuli/status/2106412329680154957 and wondered why its so slow. I had one opus 5.5 and one Astra 6 High agent check it out and reproduce it and basically the commit #18508 seems to cause a major slowdown. I had them prepare 2 repl environments to personally verify it as far as I see it they found a verifiable issue. I linked them in Reproduction. Otherwise thank you for your good work and I wish you a pleasant day! (2 Repl links in Reproduction, hand tested across 2 browsers and reported both system infos. Below the AI description (unverified)) The numbers you see in the AI Issue description are reported on the AIBOX (Proxmox host, aibox vm inside, 16 cores, rest is in System info). 

AI Issue description: 
**Summary**

Since 5.57.1, many writes to one `$state` before a flush are much slower when the state is read through a function call in the template, e.g. `{fmt(count)}`. That compiles to one derived per consumer. With 1000 rows, 10,000 writes and one flush: about 28 ms on 5.57.0, about 360–460 ms on 5.57.1 (headless Chromium, production build). A direct read like `` {`[${count}]`} `` is not affected, and one write per flush is not affected. The rendered output is always correct; only the bookkeeping grows.

**Bisect** (clean `git revert` / `cherry-pick` applied to the npm package, same component, median ms):

| Runtime | ms |
|---|---:|
| 5.57.0 | 27.8 |
| 5.57.0 + #18127 | 175.1 |
| 5.57.0 + #18508 | 28.8 |
| 5.57.0 + #18127 + #18508 | 365.8 |
| 5.57.1 | 355.6 |
| 5.57.1 − #18127 | 29.0 |
| 5.57.1 − #18508 | 174.6 |
| main `7c2fcdae6` | 440.9 |
| main − #18127 | 28.7 |

So #18127 starts it, and #18508 (same release) roughly doubles it. #18508 alone has no effect.

**What we think happens**

1. **#18127:** `WAS_MARKED` let `mark_reactions` skip a derived that was already marked since the last flush. Now every write recurses into all 1000 deriveds. The render effect behind each derived is only `MAYBE_DIRTY`, so the `(flags & DIRTY) === 0` check passes and the effect is scheduled again on every write (`reactivity/sources.js` around lines 380–409 in 5.57.1). The new `seen` set is reset on every write and only used above 100,000 deps in one traversal, so it never activates here.
2. **#18508:** `schedule()` used to walk up and stop at an already-marked branch, so a duplicate cost O(1). Now it pushes to `#scheduled`, and `#resolve()` walks every entry, duplicates included. The duplicates from (1) become a 10,000,000-entry array at flush.

Counters from instrumented copies (1000 rows, 10,000 writes, one flush):

| | 5.57.0 | 5.57.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `mark_reactions` calls | 11,000 | 10,010,000 |
| `schedule` calls | 1,000 | 10,000,000 |
| peak `#scheduled` length | 1,000 (with #18508 only) | 10,000,000 |
| derived executions / effect runs | 1,000 / 1,000 | 1,000 / 1,000 |

**Scaling** (1000 rows, slowdown 5.57.1 vs 5.57.0 by writes per flush): 1 → about 1×, 100 → 2.6×, 1,000 → 8×, 10,000 → about 13×. The time per write stays O(rows), with a constant about 10× larger. The memory for `#scheduled` grows from O(rows) to O(rows × writes).

**Context**

- Still present on main (`7c2fcdae6`) and on the open PR #18861.
- The review of #18127 already showed a slowdown on a different graph (10 wide, 10 deep, one increment): https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/18127#discussion_r3242505605. This report is a different shape: a flat fan-out with many writes per flush.
- #18123, which #18127 links, was already fixed by #18124. Its `derived-dep-set-while-rendering` fixture still passes with #18127 reverted. That does not show a revert is safe for the async system, so we don't propose a fix.

body_text: ### Describe the bug When an element is scoped by the component's ` ``` Client output (5.57.1, `dev: false`): ```js $.set_class(span, 1, 'b [&>*]:a svelte-n50uah'); ``` The server output is correct, since the browser decodes the entity when it parses the HTML: ```js $$renderer.push(`span`); ``` So with SSR, the element starts with the class `b [&>*]:a svelte-n50uah`. During hydration, `set_class` sees that its value differs from the server attribute and writes `b [&>*]:a svelte-n50uah`. Without SSR, the class is wrong from the start. In our app this broke Tailwind arbitrary variants such as `[&>*:first-child]:shrink-0` after hydration, and the result was a layout shift. The value has to compile to a string literal that goes to `set_class`. I found four ways that happens: - an interpolation whose values the compiler can evaluate: a `const` string, a `let` or `$state` that is never reassigned, a module-level `const`, or an inline string (`class="b {'[&>*]:a'}"`); - a string literal written as an expression: `class={'b [&>*]:a'}`; - static class text on an element that also has a `class:` directive; - static class text on a custom element, or on a `` with no other attributes and no `style:` directives. The escaping arrived in 5.20.3 (#15352). Interpolated `const` and `let` values have reached it since 5.27.0, when partial evaluation was added (#15494). These are not affected: - elements without scoped styles, because no hash is appended and the literal is passed unescaped; - static class text on a regular element without `class:` directives, which is written into the template markup; - elements with spread attributes, and `` with other attributes or `style:` directives, which use `attribute_effect` with the raw value; - a single expression that isn't a string literal, such as `class={X}` or ``class={`b ${X}`}``, because it isn't folded; - other attributes (`title`, `data-*`, `style`), whose folded values are passed to `set_attribute` / `set_style` unescaped. The cause is `build_set_class` in `packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/client/visitors/shared/element.js`, added in #15352: ```js value = b.literal(escape_html(value.value, true) + ' ' + context.state.analysis.css.hash); ``` Escaping is right for values written into template markup, but this literal only ever goes to `set_class`. I intend to submit a PR that removes the `escape_html` call. ### Reproduction [Playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/untitled#H4sIAAAAAAAAE22P0U7DMAxFf8WyEANUte9Zmokf4AeWPaSpJyJlaVSbwVTl31GiAS-8xMq51_b1hsldCBX66JiB2LtMM3Z4DpEY1XFDueVqqAC7H_trzj1fKUplk2P6j_slCSVhVKjZryGLscmKXxILXN0aXBIYYXd8NC8n5Xb7qkYS4OwSjPDA4oSenvc26eFvQNJNn0KalbwHHrf6L9BOGC1OsN2HF4umanqor7FJZ9Ncb-5CCrRfZjKt-9D_8qKHxvWQ79vkFqkl7yfYaq03xGVVsNLcQpeW8O7DDoW-BJWsH1ROHYoL8TOkGdXZRabyDZ0XDml1AQAA). It renders `className: b [&>*]:a svelte-n50uah`, and the compiled JS passes the escaped literal to `$.set_class`. ### Logs _No response_ ### System Info ```shell svelte 5.57.1 (also reproduced on main at 7c2fcdae6). The problem is in the compiler output, so it does not depend on the OS or browser. ``` ### Severity annoyance

### Describe the bug On a `$state` object, assigning a key that the object only inherits from its prototype (`toString`, `valueOf`, `constructor`, `hasOwnProperty` and so on) does nothing. The value isn't stored anywhere. The key still reads as the inherited function, `Object.hasOwn` returns `false`, and `Object.keys`, `JSON.stringify`, `$state.snapshot` and object spread all leave it out. On a plain object the same assignment creates an own property. ```js const state = $state({}); state.toString = 'own'; state.toString; // the inherited function (a plain object gives 'own') Object.hasOwn(state, 'toString'); // false (true) JSON.stringify(state); // '{}' ('{"toString":"own"}') ``` A key that is present when the state is created can be reassigned normally (`$state({ toString: 'a' })`, then `state.toString = 'b'`). Only adding one later is affected. Deleting such a key has the opposite problem. After `delete state.toString`, `state.toString` reads `undefined` and `'toString' in state` returns `false`, so `String(state)` throws. That happens whether or not the object ever had an own `toString`. On a plain object the inherited member shows through again. This also makes server and client disagree. During SSR `$state` is a plain object, so a write made while the component initialises is kept on the server and dropped on the client: `

{JSON.stringify(state)}

` after `state.toString = 'own'` renders `{"toString":"own"}` on the server and `{}` once hydrated. SvelteKit 3 supports a remote form field named `toString` (sveltejs/kit#17134, fixed in sveltejs/kit#17136). The client keeps the form's value in a `$state` object, though, so with `@sveltejs/kit` 3.0.1 and `svelte` 5.57.2: - text typed into `` never reaches `form.fields.toString.value()` or `form.fields.value()`; - `form.fields.toString.set('hello')` never reaches the input, so the form submits `toString: ""`. The cause is in the proxy's `set` trap. It decides whether the key is new with `prop in target`, which is `true` for an inherited key. When the key has no source yet, a source is only created if the key is new or has a writable own descriptor, and an inherited key is neither. The trap doesn't write to the target either, so the value is lost. `ownKeys` has the same `in` check, so it wouldn't list such a key even if it were stored. And `Object.hasOwn(state, 'toString')`, which #18838 made reactive through the `has` trap, still tracks nothing for an inherited key, because `has` doesn't create a source for one. Notes from trying to fix it. Making the write land is simple: create the key's source when the key is inherited as a writable data property, and list it in `ownKeys`. These constraints are what I couldn't get past without regressions: - `Object.hasOwn(state, 'toString')` needs to become reactive too. Tracking it through the object's version loops: an effect that checks it and deletes another key re-runs until `effect_update_depth_exceeded`, because `deleteProperty` increments the version even when the key is already gone. - Forks. A new key's source starts as `undefined`, so discarding a fork that assigned `state.toString` leaves an own `toString` holding `undefined`. Ordinary keys already behave like that: after a discarded fork they stay in `Object.keys`. For keys created by an assignment, two changes together fixed the discard cases I tested: starting new sources as `UNINITIALIZED`, and falling back to the prototype in `get` and `has`. But `has` and `ownKeys` check `source.v`. Inside the fork the key then disappears from `in` and `Object.keys` while `state.x` still reads it. - Non-extensible targets (`$state(Object.freeze({}))`). Storing the key makes `ownKeys` report a key the target can't have, so `Object.keys` throws. I'm happy to open a PR if there's a preferred direction. ### Reproduction [Playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/hello-world?version=5.57.2#H4sIAAAAAAAAE4WOUUuFQBCF_8owBCqIvtu60Fv0kA_3MXtYdexubbPizs0u4n8PFSki6G34zvkOMyObd8IC78k5D5MfXQcxdVaoSzDF3joKWDzNKNdh7a0A08O6G4YsfJCTlTUm0F-89SzEErBAFdrRDqJrrsWRQBAjBCXcbEc8L8ltzSr_brFqLiKewXPrbPtWznECpYZ4EzLxJxktv0AJkZ84ShYdSODAKt9t_d-OlzONv0Y29mOhZjXo-eFUPWZhW7f9ddeTReWD3vOqeaVWsrMJ1cR7nEJ0PBTtVUxR6FOwkPFCy3OKYqybLHdY9MYFWr4A3qtuSJcBAAA) ```svelte

{JSON.stringify(state)}

{Object.hasOwn(state, 'toString')}

``` Click "set toString", then "set other". Expected: `{"toString":"own"}` and `true`, then `{"toString":"own","other":"own"}` and `true`. Actual: `{}` and `false`, then `{"other":"own"}` and `false`. ### Logs ```shell n/a (no error; the assignment is ignored) ``` ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 27.2 CPU: (18) arm64 Apple M5 Pro Memory: 6.45 GB / 64.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 24.16.0 npm: 11.13.0 pnpm: 11.28.3 Browsers: Chrome: 154.0.8037.98 Safari: 27.2 npmPackages: @sveltejs/kit: 3.0.1 => 3.0.1 svelte: 5.57.2 => 5.57.2 ``` Also reproduced on `main` at 10fdca7d7. ### Severity annoyance

### Describe the bug

If a user types into a server-rendered `<input {value}>` (no `bind:`) before hydration has finished, Svelte 5 resets the input to the server-rendered value as soon as it hydrates.

I first noticed that a remote form's `<input {...form.field.as(...) />` was doing this and have narrowed it down to this as the cause.

Very similar to #18928 but for inputs and `bind:` is unaffected in this case.

### Reproduction

The reproduction uses `hooks.client.ts` to delay hydration so you have 5 seconds to type something into the input before it disappears:

https://stackblitz.com/github/nathanlindsay/svelte-hydration-overrides-input-value

### Describe the bug With `experimental.async`, if a component with a top-level `await` is inside a `` without `pending`, `onMount` / `$effect` in its children run while the DOM is still in the offscreen fragment (`isConnected` is `false`, sizes are 0). It gets attached right after. Prod build only, dev is fine. Every SvelteKit app with async hits this, since `root.svelte` wraps each route in a ``. In our case a bottom sheet that sets `scrollTop` in `onMount` stays hidden after a reload. Looks like `Batch.schedule()` only checks `effect.b.is_pending` and ignores pending ancestors. ### Reproduction https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/z6n3sx ```svelte ``` ```svelte ``` ```svelte
{data}
``` `vite build && vite preview` logs `false`, `vite dev` logs `true`. Without the boundary it's `true` in both. `tick()` / `settled()` inside `onMount` don't help in SvelteKit either. This fixes it for us (repro + our app): ```js // Batch.schedule() var boundary = effect.b; while (boundary && !boundary.is_pending) boundary = boundary.parent; if (boundary && (effect.f & (EFFECT | RENDER_EFFECT | MANAGED_EFFECT)) !== 0 && (effect.f & REACTION_RAN) === 0) { boundary.defer_effect(effect); return; } ``` ### Logs ```shell ``` ### System Info ```shell svelte 5.57.1 (same code in 5.57.2), @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte 7.3.1, vite 8.3.2, @sveltejs/kit 3.0.0, Chrome ``` ### Severity blocking all usage of svelte

### Describe the bug `a11y_no_noninteractive_tabindex` fires when an element's `role` and `tabindex` are both chosen by the same condition, even though every branch is valid: the element is a non-focusable `img` in one branch and a focusable interactive role in the other. The checker only reads static `role` values, so any `role={...}` expression is treated as non-interactive. It does not look at the branches, and it does not see that `tabindex` is only set in the interactive branch. Real case: a chart that is a static image while loading, disabled or empty, and a keyboard-operable inspector otherwise. ### Reproduction ```svelte
event.key === 'Enter' && onselect()} >
``` Warning (5.56.10 and 5.57.2): `a11y_no_noninteractive_tabindex: noninteractive element cannot have nonnegative tabIndex value`. Expected: no warning. Both pairs are valid: `img` without a `tabindex`, and `button` with `tabindex="0"`. A possible fix: when `role` is a conditional expression with static string branches, check each branch against the static `tabindex`, or against the matching branch of a `tabindex` conditional with the same test. Only do this when evaluating the test twice must give the same result: `$derived`/`$state`/plain local bindings and literals combined with `!`, `&&`, `||`, `===` (no calls, property reads, coercing operators, props or globals, since each read of a prop runs the parent's getter). Treat `undefined` as absent only when it is not a local binding. Keep warning when: - `role={inert ? 'img' : 'button'} tabindex="0"` should still warn. - Different tests for `role` and `tabindex` should still warn. - `role={f() ? 'img' : 'button'} tabindex={f() ? undefined : 0}` should still warn. For comparison, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y's recommended config (`allowExpressionValues: true`) does not report expression roles at all. ### Logs _No response_ ### System Info ```shell svelte 5.56.10, also reproduced with 5.57.2 (compile with generate: false) ``` ### Severity annoyance

### Describe the bug A component that reads `$effect.pending()` inside a `$derived` is never garbage collected after it unmounts, and neither is anything that derived closes over. `$state.eager()` in a `$derived` does the same. Reading `$effect.pending()` directly in the template doesn't leak. I think this is the cause: `$effect.pending()` compiles to `$.eager(() => $.pending())`, and `eager()` in `src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js` keeps the reaction that reads it in a module-level `version_map`. The teardown only removes it when the reaction is being destroyed: ```js let parent = active_reaction; let version = version_map.get(parent) ?? source(0); version_map.set(parent, version); teardown(() => { if (parent.f & DESTROYING) version_map.delete(parent); }); ``` A render effect gets `DESTROYING` when its component unmounts, so that entry goes away. A derived never gets that flag, so its entry stays forever, and the map keeps the derived, its `fn` and everything that closes over alive. I ran into this in a SvelteKit app where a data table's loading state was `$derived((hydrated && $effect.pending() > 0) || isStale(...))`. Every visit to a list page kept the previous visit's table, with all its rows and cells, in memory. Heap snapshots showed the retaining path `version_map → derived → fn → closure → table`. Replacing the `$effect.pending()` read fixed it. Possibly related: with that same derived on the page, client-side navigation from it to a page with layerchart charts behind a top-level `await` hung the tab at 100% CPU in development (not in a production build) until it ran out of memory. That also went away without the `$effect.pending()` read. I haven't reduced that one to a small reproduction. ### Reproduction body_text:
### Describe the bug

Reactive writes immediately before hydration can make an async component tree read stale state and fail during hydration

The original report uses SvelteKit 3.0.1 / Svelte 5.57.2. Kit applies loaded `data` and `child` to an existing reactive root immediately before hydrating. With an async expression, a pending boundary, and a nested effect reading derived layout data, hydration fails.

### Reproduction

Original Kit reproduction: https://github.com/Tinggaard/sveltekit3-root-properties-undefined
Original report: https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/17383

Run:

```sh
FILTER=async-hydration-pre-mount-writes pnpm test runtime-runes
```

### Describe the problem

On my application, I have various global caches containing the data needed to render Things as a $signal.raw. Whenever I need to show a Thing, I can load it from the cache to make sure every instance of the Thing is the same, even across updates to the Thing.

However, it's currently not that easy to know when the data can be garbage collected away. The best way to accomplish this in a supported way is to create an $effect for every reference into the cache and keep track of the reference counts alongside. This *works* but doesn't feel optimal especially considering *Svelte is already aware of this information*. It can also result in attempting to call $effect outside a component if the implementation tries to be clever.

If I'm fine with meddling with Svelte internals and accept it possibly breaking under me without notice, I can postprocess the Svelte compiler output to get access to the signal object, where I can check `.reactions?.length > 0` for a, what seems like quite accurate, reference count and an "is used" flag for that signal.

### Describe the proposed solution

Svelte should provide the ability to get either a reference count, or an "is used" flag, for any $state (and perhaps $derived?)

I'm not entirely sure what use cases knowing the exact reference count would be useful for and how accurate it would be when combined with other features current or planned, but it would be more flexible compared to "is used" (which would just be `refcount > 0`, but refcount would not need to be accurate above 1)

If a formal definition of how a signal is considered "used" is needed, I would expect "has any $effect that depends on it or another signal derived from it" to cover most use cases (as I believe templates compile down to $effect as well), but I'm not too well versed in Svelte internals to know if there are any flaws in this definition.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

On the server, when a child writes to a prop bound by its parent (`bind:value`) during render, the parent's template is rendered again until bindings settle (the `$$settled` / `copy()` / `subsume()` loop). The first pass is thrown away, but the `onDestroy` callbacks registered by components in that pass are thrown away with it and never run. Only the final pass's callbacks are collected.

Anything a component sets up during render and releases in `onDestroy` therefore leaks once per request. The common case is a manual `store.subscribe()` on a module-level store: the subscriber (and the component state its callback closes over) is retained for the lifetime of the process. In our app this was an SSR heap OOM within about a minute of taking production traffic.

This is the same family as #18584 (fixed in #18585) and #18975, but a different path: nothing throws here, the pass is discarded on purpose.

### Describe the bug

Vite can pass `undefined` to an HMR accept callback when the updated module fails to load ([Vite docs](https://vite.dev/guide/api-hmr#hot-accept-cb)). Svelte reads `module.default` without checking it, causing a second error in HMR.

The callback should return early when the module is undefined. Fix proposed in #19002.

### Reproduction

[Minimal Svelte + Vite project](https://gist.github.com/CoderSerio/90cddcc678c44463dd586729c43e0daf)

1. Download the files, run `npm install` and `npm run dev`.
2. Open the app and browser console.
3. Add `throw new Error("failed update");` inside `<script module>` in `App.svelte` and save without refreshing.

Besides the expected `failed update` error, the HMR callback throws:

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default')
    at App.svelte:26:28
```

### System Info

Svelte 5.57.1, Vite 8.2.1, @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte 7.1.2, Node 22.22.0, macOS 26.5.1, Chromium 155.

### Severity

### Describe the bug

https://github.com/FreHu/svelte-effect-walk-repro 
has the full writeup and repro/suggested fix runnable as npm commands.

In our app, a table renders rows with `{#each}`, and a row can open a nested table, which can open another one. Each table is a component with about 70 `$derived` values built from its `rows` prop, many of them reading the same earlier ones. A slice of it, with the real names:

```js
const converted = $derived(addConvertedColumns(projected.rows, conversions));
const rows = $derived(converted.rows);
const convertedFrom = $derived(new Map(/* … from converted.columns */));
const allColumns = $derived(/* withProjections, convertedFrom, converted.columns */);
// … available, columns and activeFilters follow from allColumns
const filtered = $derived(filterRows(applyFilters(rows, activeFilters), columns, query));
const sorted = $derived(activeSort ? sortRows(filtered, activeSort.column, activeSort.dir) : filtered);
const tree = $derived(treeOn ? buildTree(sorted /* … */) : undefined);
const lines = $derived(tree ? visibleNodes(tree, isOpen) : sorted.map(toLine));
const pageCount = $derived(Math.ceil(lines.length / pageSize));
const current = $derived(Math.min(page, pageCount - 1));
const visible = $derived(lines.slice(current * pageSize, (current + 1) * pageSize));
```

That slice alone has three diamonds, each a pair of paths that split and meet again:

- `converted` reaches `filtered` both through `rows` and through `convertedFrom` → `allColumns` → `columns`.
- `sorted` reaches `lines` both directly and through `tree`.
- `lines` reaches `visible` both directly and through `pageCount` → `current`.

Every diamond doubles the number of paths from the top to `visible`. The cells `visible` renders pass row data into the nested table's props, so its own diamonds multiply the count again.

Once a minute a clock updates for relative dates, and the tables get new row objects. With three tables nested inside each other (about 50 rows in all), that one update blocked the main thread for **129 seconds**, every minute. Nothing was in a loop: no error, no warning, and it finished on its own.

A profile put 98% of the time in `schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation`.

### Describe the bug In a keyed `{#each}`, when one update removes several items and some of their outros take no time (`duration: 0`, or a transition function that returns no duration) while others do, none of the removed items is ever taken out of the DOM. They stay `inert`, at their final transition state, until the component is destroyed. If every removed item has a timed outro, or every one has none, they are removed as expected. The cause is in `pause_effects` (`packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/blocks/each.js`). An outro of zero duration finishes synchronously, inside the loop that starts the outros, before `group` exists. Its callback takes the `else` branch and only decrements `remaining`. After the loop, `remaining` is not zero, so `group` is created with `pending: new Set(to_destroy)`, which still holds the effect that already finished. Nothing removes it from `pending` again, so `pending.size` never reaches 0 and `destroy_effects` never runs for the group. We hit this with an `animate:` + `out:` grid whose outro duration depends on the item. I intend to submit a PR for this. ### Reproduction [Playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/untitled#H4sIAAAAAAAAE22QzW6rMBCFX-XUrdREIiFNuqJA1Re42y5CFg4MwiqMqT2kt0J-9yvD_dlcr2aOZz6f41m1pievsvOs5HsklS2CShTrIXZv47j3N-olalft6X96bVmIxatM5b52ZpSy4krMMFonmNHqhhDQOjvgcd1KxWn2Rozlx5eK43hPAiM0eBR48KKFNuenBMcEp8v2peI8_cfm_DqJWIblujf1RzFvtihKbP4Azk-XbSgdDfZGOEJzg1Oerksr4G63w3Gx5mEnQWsdDoNPcFrK58PSxMWrlQ496RvBMKQjeD0QprHRQvuKEc8PMtKRg_GgGzmsTzd7vBvpQJ-T7tFMTsfEPlmZ2tEeu11Z8XxPuu5-x9d-KdYw2xD_Jh-jxyy6Leb5LyhbB4uiwBGvOCCLvhFCOceLkKdjhKcRHipWiRL6KSoTN1G4JEq06b8MNyprde8p_AL8t156DwIAAA) ```svelte {#each items as item (item)}

{item}

{/each} ``` Click the button: `2` and `3` are never removed. With `duration: 400` for both, they are. ### Logs ```shell None: no error is thrown. ``` ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 26.5.2 CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M5 Binaries: Node: 25.9.0 pnpm: 11.12.0 Browsers: Chrome: 155.0.8059.82 npmPackages: svelte: 5.57.0, and reproduced on main (40bb084) ``` ### Severity annoyance

### Describe the bug

Assigning to a writable `$derived` after one of its dependencies has changed, but before it has been re-read, is silently ignored when the assigned value equals the **stale** cached value. The next read recomputes and the override is lost.

```js
let source = $state(1);
let value = $derived(source);

value;      // read once, cached value is 1
source = 2; // value is now stale
value = 1;  // equals the stale cached 1 → no-op
value;      // → 2, expected 1
```

The write happens after the dependency change, so per the documented semantics (an override holds until a dependency changes) it should win. Assigning any other value (e.g. `value = 5`) works as expected; only a value equal to the stale cache is dropped.

Happens both when the derived is connected (read in an effect/template) and disconnected.

https://svelte.dev/playground/80da0a3235c34c209afd8536ef8f99f2?version=5.57.2

body_text:
### Describe the bug

Since 5.57.1 (#18733), the server turns `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked` on `<input>` into `value`/`checked`, including when they come from a spread. Other places where the client supports these props don't get this on the server:

- `<textarea {...props}>`: a spread `defaultValue` is output as a lowercase `defaultvalue="..."` attribute, and the textarea is empty. A spread `value` is output as a `value="..."` attribute, which textareas ignore.
- `<svelte:element this="input">`: a spread `defaultChecked` is output as `defaultchecked="true"`. A static `defaultChecked` is dropped. The same happens with `defaultValue`, and with `defaultValue` on `<svelte:element this="textarea">`.

The client sets the value when it hydrates. Before hydration, or without JavaScript, these textareas are empty and these checkboxes are unchecked.

The open PRs #18771 and #18911 fix static `<textarea defaultValue>`, but both leave spreads out and only handle regular elements. I ran into this in a component library that forwards props with `{...rest}`.

The cause seems to be that the server decides at compile time, from a literal `<input>`, whether these props get special handling (code on `main`, unchanged since 5.57.2):

- Spread path: `prepare_element_spread` only sets `ELEMENT_IS_INPUT` for a regular `<input>` ([shared/element.js#L476-L482](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2334f5ed0bc9628fddd9767a92f7f12c09e50cd5/packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/shared/element.js#L476-L482)). `$.attributes()` only maps `defaultvalue`/`defaultchecked` when that flag is set. Without the flag it outputs them as attributes ([internal/server/index.js#L166-L178](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2334f5ed0bc9628fddd9767a92f7f12c09e50cd5/packages/svelte/src/internal/server/index.js#L166-L178)). It also returns only attributes, so a spread can't set a textarea's content.
- Static path: `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked` are kept only on a regular `<input>` and dropped everywhere else, including `<svelte:element>` ([shared/element.js#L83-L92](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2334f5ed0bc9628fddd9767a92f7f12c09e50cd5/packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/shared/element.js#L83-L92)).

### Reproduction

[Playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/untitled?version=5.57.2#H4sIAAAAAAAAE5WQQU-EMBCF_8pkLlwI3CuQGP-Bm3ixHgoMbmN3SuiwYgj_3RSXoOjFW_vyzbz3ZkY2F0KFLXVmdPJk3Ej57fNwpuaNWrAMoR_ItAHacbD8CqfTI6bYWUcB1fOM8tHHJVHAdFt53_dZuJKTqNUm0F9641mIJaDCIjSD7aXSrKXxHASEJoESZvieTkFyJud8AsvdjtZ-WsmYREHSxOi1n5IUfpZRIMNI62iR74ZcWO5HgTnLsui6QF5pLuLTDGR2vSryTfwFzHA9BDziu0ntp5vH1ykUOboQC8jZhlLjSmr8Fxu7lxq37hoP3dcdmGJMhCreYXlJUYx175ZbVJ1xgZZPBuq05BMCAAA). The playground doesn't server-render, but "JS output" with `generate: "server"` shows the compiled code.

```svelte
<script>
	const text = { defaultValue: 'hello' };
	const box = { type: 'checkbox', defaultChecked: true };
</script>

<input {...text} />
<textarea {...text}></textarea>
<textarea {...{ value: 'hello' }}></textarea>
<input {...box} />
<svelte:element this="input" {...box} />
<svelte:element this="input" type="checkbox" defaultChecked />
```

Render it with `svelte/server` (`npm i svelte@5.57.2`, save the component as `App.svelte`, then run `node repro.mjs`):

```js
// repro.mjs
import { compile } from 'svelte/compiler';
import { render } from 'svelte/server';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const { js } = compile(readFileSync('App.svelte', 'utf8'), { generate: 'server', filename: 'App.svelte' });
writeFileSync('App.server.mjs', js.code);
const { default: App } = await import('./App.server.mjs');
console.log(render(App).body);
```

Actual output (hydration comments removed, one element per line):

```html
<input value="hello"/>
<textarea defaultvalue="hello"></textarea>
<textarea value="hello"></textarea>
<input type="checkbox" checked=""/>
<input type="checkbox" defaultchecked="true">
<input type="checkbox">
```

Expected:

```html
<input value="hello"/>
<textarea>hello</textarea>
<textarea>hello</textarea>
<input type="checkbox" checked=""/>
<input type="checkbox" checked="">
<input type="checkbox" checked="">
```

Lines 1 and 4 show that the same objects already work on a regular `<input>`. `defaultValue` is typed on `<textarea>` (`HTMLTextareaAttributes`), and the `form-default-value-spread` runtime test covers spread `defaultValue` on textareas on the client. Since 5.57.1 (#18733), the server turns `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked` on `<input>` into `value`/`checked`, including when they come from a spread. Other places where the client supports these props don't get this on the server:

- `<textarea {...props}>`: a spread `defaultValue` is output as a lowercase `defaultvalue="..."` attribute, and the textarea is empty. A spread `value` is output as a `value="..."` attribute, which textareas ignore.
- `<svelte:element this="input">`: a spread `defaultChecked` is output as `defaultchecked="true"`. A static `defaultChecked` is dropped. The same happens with `defaultValue`, and with `defaultValue` on `<svelte:element this="textarea">`.

The client sets the value when it hydrates. Before hydration, or without JavaScript, these textareas are empty and these checkboxes are unchecked.

The open PRs #18771 and #18911 fix static `<textarea defaultValue>`, but both leave spreads out and only handle regular elements. I ran into this in a component library that forwards props with `{...rest}`.

The cause seems to be that the server decides at compile time, from a literal `<input>`, whether these props get special handling (code on `main`, unchanged since 5.57.2):

- Spread path: `prepare_element_spread` only sets `ELEMENT_IS_INPUT` for a regular `<input>` ([shared/element.js#L476-L482](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2334f5ed0bc9628fddd9767a92f7f12c09e50cd5/packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/shared/element.js#L476-L482)). `$.attributes()` only maps `defaultvalue`/`defaultchecked` when that flag is set. Without the flag it outputs them as attributes ([internal/server/index.js#L166-L178](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2334f5ed0bc9628fddd9767a92f7f12c09e50cd5/packages/svelte/src/internal/server/index.js#L166-L178)). It also returns only attributes, so a spread can't set a textarea's content.
- Static path: `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked` are kept only on a regular `<input>` and dropped everywhere else, including `<svelte:element>` ([shared/element.js#L83-L92](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2334f5ed0bc9628fddd9767a92f7f12c09e50cd5/packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/shared/element.js#L83-L92)).

	const box = { type: 'checkbox', defaultChecked: true };
</script>

<input {...text} />

## Feature Description
_(This issue may apply equally to plain swagger-maven-plugin, I haven't tested)_

By default the plugin does not understand Kotlin well:
- non-nullable fields are not automatically listed as required. 
- field names starting with 'is' will lose their prefix in the doc, which is simply wrong.
- there may be other discrepancies

I would like a solution to this that requires as little effort and awareness as possible of the developer. 

## Use Case

I want to write my endpoints and dtos in standard kotlin, with as little though as possible to the quirks of my documentation tool, and for the plugin to extract as much knowledge as possible from the code before needing annotations.

## Suggested Solution (optional)

The solution should leverage jackson's kotlin module, which understands all the problematic cases well.

Some implementation alternatives - in order of prefence:
1. The plugin uses kotlin-module by default for Kotlin classes
2. A separate plugin is provided that supports Kotlin
3. A simple config option for enabling Kotlin support
4. Include a ready-made KotlinAwareObjectMapperProcessor that just needs to be configured i the pom

## Alternatives Considered

- The standard solution is to provide the plugin with a custom objectMapperProcessorClass that registers jackson's kotlin module to the mapper.  This is a small task and works well, but feels unnecessary (especially writing the processor yourself), and more importantly:
   - You get no hint that you need to do this, until someone discovers the docs are wrong.
- Explicit tagging can fix it, but it is not intuitive that you need to, since the information is right there in the code. Even when you know, it is easy to forget, and the resulting error is hard to spot.

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-core/issues) to ensure this is not a duplicate.
- [x] This feature would be useful to more than just my use case.
- [x] I have provided enough detail for the maintainers to understand the scope of the request.

_(This issue may apply equally to plain swagger-maven-plugin, I haven't tested)_

By default the plugin does not understand Kotlin well:
- non-nullable fields are not automatically listed as required. 
- field names starting with 'is' will lose their prefix in the doc, which is simply wrong.
- there may be other discrepancies

I would like a solution to this that requires as little effort and awareness as possible of the developer. 

## Use Case

I want to write my endpoints and dtos in standard kotlin, with as little though as possible to the quirks of my documentation tool, and for the plugin to extract as much knowledge as possible from the code before needing annotations.

## Suggested Solution (optional)

The solution should leverage jackson's kotlin module, which understands all the problematic cases well.

Some implementation alternatives - in order of prefence:
1. The plugin uses kotlin-module by default for Kotlin classes
2. A separate plugin is provided that supports Kotlin
3. A simple config option for enabling Kotlin support
4. Include a ready-made KotlinAwareObjectMapperProcessor that just needs to be configured i the pom

## Alternatives Considered

- The standard solution is to provide the plugin with a custom objectMapperProcessorClass that registers jackson's kotlin module to the mapper.  This is a small task and works well, but feels unnecessary (especially writing the processor yourself), and more importantly:
   - You get no hint that you need to do this, until someone discovers the docs are wrong.
- Explicit tagging can fix it, but it is not intuitive that you need to, since the information is right there in the code. Even when you know, it is easy to forget, and the resulting error is hard to spot.

- [x] This feature would be useful to more than just my use case.
- [x] I have provided enough detail for the maintainers to understand the scope of the request.
