### Which project does this relate to? Start ### Describe the bug In `renderRouterToStream.tsx`, the `onError` callback added in #5996 destroys the `PassThrough` stream on **any** error, including errors that are caught by React Error Boundaries (recoverable errors). React's `renderToPipeableStream` calls `onError` for **all** errors — both recoverable (caught by Error Boundary) and unrecoverable. When the error is recoverable: 1. Error Boundary catches the error and renders `errorComponent` / `defaultErrorComponent` 2. `onShellReady` fires normally — the shell includes the error fallback UI 3. `onError` also fires → **`stream.destroy()` kills the already-piping stream** 4. Response body becomes broken → upstream proxy returns **502 Bad Gateway** This means `defaultErrorComponent` and route-level `errorComponent` never render during SSR — users always see a 502 instead of the intended error page. ### Your Example Website or App N/A (reproducible in any TanStack Start app with `defaultErrorComponent` set) ### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue 1. Set `defaultErrorComponent` in `createRouter()`: ```ts const router = createRouter({ routeTree, defaultErrorComponent: () => , }) ``` 2. Throw an error in any route component: ```tsx function RouteComponent() { throw new Error('test error') return
Hello
} ``` 3. Access the page via SSR → 502 Bad Gateway instead of MyErrorPage ### Expected behavior The Error Boundary should catch the error and render defaultErrorComponent during SSR, returning a valid HTML response (with status 500). ### Screenshots or Videos _No response_ ### Platform @tanstack/react-router: 1.167.16 (any version after #5996 merge on 2025-11-29) @tanstack/react-start: 1.167.16 ### Additional context #### Root Cause In [packages/react-router/src/ssr/renderRouterToStream.tsx](https://github.com/TanStack/router/blob/main/packages/react-router/src/ssr/renderRouterToStream.tsx): ```ts onError: (error, info) => { console.error('Error in renderToPipeableStream:', error, info) // Destroy the passthrough stream on error if (!reactAppPassthrough.destroyed) { reactAppPassthrough.destroy( error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)), ) } }, ``` #### Proposed Fix Follow [React's recommended pattern](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/server/renderToPipeableStream#setting-the-status-code): ```ts onShellError(error) { console.error('SSR Shell Error:', error) if (!reactAppPassthrough.destroyed) reactAppPassthrough.destroy( error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)), ) }, onError: (error, info) => { console.error('Error in renderToPipeableStream:', error, info) }, ``` - `onError`: logging/flag-setting only, no `stream.destroy()`. This aligns with [React's recommended pattern](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/server/renderToPipeableStream#setting-the-status-code) where `onError` is used solely for logging — none of React's official examples destroy the stream in `onError`. - `onShellError` (new): handle unrecoverable shell errors with fallback HTML, as documented in React's API reference.

### Which project does this relate to?

Start

### Describe the bug

The TanStack Start Vite plugin and the Router CLI write different `routeTree.gen.ts` files for the same project, and the scaffold produced by `tanstack create` ships both.

The Start plugin (`@tanstack/start-plugin-core`, `start-router-plugin/route-tree-footer.ts`) appends a footer to the generated route tree:

```ts
import type { getRouter } from './router.tsx'
import type { createStart } from '@tanstack/react-start'
declare module '@tanstack/react-start' {
  interface Register {
    ssr: true
    router: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getRouter>>
  }
}
```

`tsr generate` (`@tanstack/router-cli`) does not know about Start and writes the file without it. So every `vite build` or `vite dev` adds the nine lines and every `tsr generate` removes them. In a project that commits `routeTree.gen.ts`, the file flips on every run of whichever tool ran last.

The scaffold's `router.tsx` still carries `declare module '@tanstack/react-router' { interface Register { router } }`, which masks the problem for the `router` registration. The `ssr: true` registration has no such fallback: after `tsr generate`, `RegisteredSsr` is `false`, so the serialisable-loader-result check (`ValidateSerializableLifecycleResult`) silently degrades to `any` until the next Vite run puts the footer back.

### Complete minimal reproducer

https://github.com/TheBinaryGuy/tanstack-start-tsr-footer-repro (the unmodified `tanstack create` output plus a `repro` script; `bun install && bun run repro` shows the diff after each step). Open in StackBlitz: https://stackblitz.com/github/TheBinaryGuy/tanstack-start-tsr-footer-repro

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

```sh
npx @tanstack/cli@latest create start-ref --framework React --package-manager bun --non-interactive --no-examples --no-toolchain --deployment nitro
cd start-ref
git add -A && git commit -qm scaffold
bun run build                 # Start plugin: routeTree.gen.ts gains the 9-line footer
git diff --stat src/routeTree.gen.ts
bun run generate-routes       # the scaffold's own `tsr generate` script: footer removed again
git diff --stat src/routeTree.gen.ts
bun run build                 # footer added again
git diff --stat src/routeTree.gen.ts
```

Observed with `@tanstack/react-start` 1.168.54, `@tanstack/start-plugin-core` 1.171.44, `@tanstack/router-cli` 1.167.36 (and the same with 1.168.49 / 1.171.39 / 1.167.33).

### Expected behavior

Both generators produce the same file for a Start project. Either `tsr generate` reads the Start footer (for example by resolving it the same way the plugin does when `@tanstack/react-start` is present), or the scaffold does not ship a `generate-routes` script that undoes what its own build writes, and the Router CLI docs say it is not for Start projects.

### Platform

- OS: macOS 27.0 (arm64)
- Bun 1.4.0, Node 24
- Vite 7

### Additional context

The Router CLI installation docs already say to use the CLI "only if you are not using a supported bundler", which suggests the fix may be on the scaffold and docs side rather than teaching the CLI about Start. A related report about the Start plugin overriding router generator configuration is #7768.

### Summary

In dev, a request to a server function whose source file this dev server has not compiled yet fails with `500 Invalid server function ID`. The validator has a recovery path meant for exactly this case, and the recovery cannot succeed: it transforms the source file under `?server-fn-module-lookup`, which is the one id the compiling transform explicitly excludes.

Versions: `@tanstack/start-plugin-core@1.171.38`, `@tanstack/react-start@1.168.48`, `vite@8.2.2`, Node 24, Windows 11. I re-read the validator in `main` today and it is unchanged.

### Where

`packages/start-plugin-core/src/vite/start-compiler-plugin/plugin.ts`, plugin `tanstack-start-core:validate-server-fn-id`:

```ts
// Trigger transform of the source file in this environment,
// which will compile createServerFn calls and populate
// serverFnsById as a side effect.
if (this.environment.mode !== 'dev') { /* … */ }

await this.environment.transformRequest(`${absPath}?${SERVER_FN_LOOKUP}`)

// Re-check after lazy compilation
if (serverFnsById[fnId]) {
  return `export {}`
}
```

### Why it cannot work

1. `serverFnsById` is written from exactly one place — `context.onServerFnsById` in `start-compiler/handleCreateServerFn.ts`, which is reachable only from `StartCompiler.compile()`.
2. The transform that calls `compile()` (`tanstack-start-core::server-fn:<env>`) is declared with `filter: { id: { exclude: new RegExp(`${SERVER_FN_LOOKUP}$`), include: TRANSFORM_ID_REGEX } }`. The recovery's id ends in `SERVER_FN_LOOKUP`, so `compile()` never runs for it.
3. The only plugin that does run on that id is `tanstack-start-core:capture-server-fn-module-lookup`, whose handler calls `compiler.ingestModule({ code, id })`. `ingestModule` is `parseAst` + `extractModuleInfo`: it populates `moduleCache`, never `serverFnsById`.

So the re-check after the transform is always false and the handler falls through to `this.error('Invalid server function ID: …')`.

`mergeServerFnsById` only ever merges, so a miss can only mean "this file has never been compiled in this dev server's lifetime" — precisely the case the comment above the recovery names ("cold restart with cached client").

### Reproduction (no browser, no HTTP request)

Boot a dev server in `middlewareMode`, render nothing, and ask the validator for an id whose file has not been compiled:

```js
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const fnId = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({
  file: '/src/path/to/your.functions.ts?tss-serverfn-split',
  export: 'yourFn_createServerFn_handler',
})).toString('base64url')

const server = await createServer({ server: { middlewareMode: true, hmr: false } })
await server.environments.ssr.transformRequest(
  `\0virtual:tanstack-start-validate-server-fn-id?id=${fnId}`,
)
// → Error: Invalid server function ID: <fnId>
```

(Note the `\0virtual:…` form rather than `/@id/__x00__virtual:…` — `/@id/` is unwrapped by the dev HTTP middleware, which `transformRequest` does not go through.)

**Control, same unpatched server, same process:** transform the clean source path first and then ask, and it resolves:

```js
await server.environments.ssr.transformRequest('/abs/path/to/your.functions.ts')
// now the validator accepts the same id
```

The only difference between the two runs is which transform ran, which also shows the shape of the fix.

In the real app this surfaced as a `500` on a POST to a server function, through `handleServerAction` → `getServerFnById`, on a dev server that had been serving for a while but had not compiled that particular module.

### Suggested fix

Transform the clean id — the one the compiling transform accepts:

```diff
 await this.environment.transformRequest(`${absPath}?${SERVER_FN_LOOKUP}`)
+if (serverFnsById[fnId]) return `export {}`
+
+await this.environment.transformRequest(absPath)
 if (serverFnsById[fnId]) return `export {}`
```

Or simply replace the lookup transform with the clean one — `compile()` does everything `ingestModule` does and registers the id as well.

I verified this locally as a `pnpm patch`. The reproduction above goes from throwing to resolving, an id with a non-existent export is still refused (so the guard still guards), and the `?tss-serverfn-split` provider module that `getServerFnById` imports right afterwards compiles and exports the handler.

Happy to open a PR if the shape above is what you'd want.

### Secondary, same handler

`if (this.environment.mode !== 'dev') this.error(…)` sits **inside** the `try { … } catch {}`. `this.error` throws, the bare `catch` swallows it, and the specific "unknown environment mode" message is replaced by the generic `Invalid server function ID`. Probably worth hoisting above the `try`.

### Which project does this relate to?

Router

### Describe the bug

### Describe the bug

`collectStaticHintsFromManifest` in `@tanstack/start-server-core` hardcodes `as: "script"` on every script hint, regardless of what `rel` the manifest helper returned.

`getScriptPreloadAttrs` in `@tanstack/router-core` correctly returns **no** `as` for the module script format — `as` is only valid alongside `rel=preload`, which is the iife branch:

```js
// @tanstack/router-core/dist/esm/manifest.js
function getScriptPreloadAttrs(manifest, link, assetCrossOrigin) {
  const preloadLink = resolveManifestAssetLink(link);
  const crossOrigin = getAssetCrossOrigin(assetCrossOrigin, "script") ?? preloadLink.crossOrigin;
  return {
    ...getManifestScriptFormat(manifest) === "iife"
      ? { rel: "preload", as: "script" }
      : { rel: "modulepreload" },          // ← no `as`, correctly
    href: preloadLink.href,
    ...crossOrigin ? { crossOrigin } : {},
  };
}
```

But the early-hints caller adds it back unconditionally:

```js
// @tanstack/start-server-core/dist/esm/early-hints.js
const attrs = getScriptPreloadAttrs(manifest, link);
const hint = {
  href: attrs.href,
  rel: attrs.rel,     // "modulepreload" for the module format
  as: "script",       // ← always added, even when rel is modulepreload
};
```

The emitted `Link` header is therefore:

```
</assets/index-abc123.js>; rel=modulepreload; as=script
```

Per the HTML spec, `modulepreload` does not take an `as` attribute — the destination is implied ("script"). Browsers register a preload that the module loader never matches, and warn a few seconds after `load`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A TanStack Start app with the default module script format and the Link header enabled.
2. Load any page and open the console.

### Expected behaviour

`modulepreload` hints are emitted without `as`, matching what `getScriptPreloadAttrs` already returns. The hint is honoured and no warning is produced.

### Actual behaviour

One warning per route chunk, on every page load. On our app that is 14 lines each load:

```
The resource https://example.com/assets/index-abc123.js was preloaded using link preload
but not used within a few seconds from the window's load event. Please make sure it wasn't
preloaded for nothing.
```

Observed in Safari 18. No functional impact — but the console becomes unusable for debugging, which is exactly where you look when something actually breaks.

### Suggested fix

Carry `as` through from the helper instead of hardcoding it:

```diff
  const attrs = getScriptPreloadAttrs(manifest, link)
  const hint = {
    href: attrs.href,
    rel: attrs.rel,
-   as: 'script',
  }
+ if (attrs.as !== undefined) hint.as = attrs.as
```

That keeps the iife path (`rel=preload; as=script`) unchanged and makes the module path spec-correct. The CSS branch below it is already correct — `rel=preload; as=style` is valid.

### Possible origin

#7327 added the Link header, and #7477 later added the iife/module split in `getScriptPreloadAttrs`. The `as: "script"` line in `early-hints.ts` looks like it predates the split and was not revisited when `rel` stopped always being `preload`.

### Versions

- `@tanstack/start-server-core` — reproduced in **1.167.22** (our deployed version, warnings observed in production) and the same code is present in **1.169.37**
- `@tanstack/router-core` 1.168.17 / 1.171.32
- `@tanstack/react-start` 1.167.50
- `@tanstack/react-router` 1.168.25
- Deployed on Cloudflare via Nitro

### Workaround

Stripping `as=script` from `modulepreload` entries in the `Link` response header, in our own server entry wrapper. The hint still works — it just becomes valid.

Router

### Describe the bug

### Describe the bug

`collectStaticHintsFromManifest` in `@tanstack/start-server-core` hardcodes `as: "script"` on every script hint, regardless of what `rel` the manifest helper returned.

`getScriptPreloadAttrs` in `@tanstack/router-core` correctly returns **no** `as` for the module script format — `as` is only valid alongside `rel=preload`, which is the iife branch:

```js
// @tanstack/router-core/dist/esm/manifest.js
function getScriptPreloadAttrs(manifest, link, assetCrossOrigin) {
  const preloadLink = resolveManifestAssetLink(link);
  const crossOrigin = getAssetCrossOrigin(assetCrossOrigin, "script") ?? preloadLink.crossOrigin;
  return {
    ...getManifestScriptFormat(manifest) === "iife"
      ? { rel: "preload", as: "script" }
      : { rel: "modulepreload" },          // ← no `as`, correctly
    href: preloadLink.href,
    ...crossOrigin ? { crossOrigin } : {},
  };
}
```

But the early-hints caller adds it back unconditionally:

```js
// @tanstack/start-server-core/dist/esm/early-hints.js
const attrs = getScriptPreloadAttrs(manifest, link);
const hint = {
  href: attrs.href,
  rel: attrs.rel,     // "modulepreload" for the module format
  as: "script",       // ← always added, even when rel is modulepreload
};
```

The emitted `Link` header is therefore:

```
</assets/index-abc123.js>; rel=modulepreload; as=script
```

Per the HTML spec, `modulepreload` does not take an `as` attribute — the destination is implied ("script"). Browsers register a preload that the module loader never matches, and warn a few seconds after `load`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A TanStack Start app with the default module script format and the Link header enabled.
2. Load any page and open the console.

### Expected behaviour

`modulepreload` hints are emitted without `as`, matching what `getScriptPreloadAttrs` already returns. The hint is honoured and no warning is produced.

### Actual behaviour

One warning per route chunk, on every page load. On our app that is 14 lines each load:

```
The resource https://example.com/assets/index-abc123.js was preloaded using link preload
but not used within a few seconds from the window's load event. Please make sure it wasn't
preloaded for nothing.
```

Observed in Safari 18. No functional impact — but the console becomes unusable for debugging, which is exactly where you look when something actually breaks.

### Suggested fix

Carry `as` through from the helper instead of hardcoding it:

```diff
  const attrs = getScriptPreloadAttrs(manifest, link)
  const hint = {
    href: attrs.href,
    rel: attrs.rel,
-   as: 'script',
  }
+ if (attrs.as !== undefined) hint.as = attrs.as
```

That keeps the iife path (`rel=preload; as=script`) unchanged and makes the module path spec-correct. The CSS branch below it is already correct — `rel=preload; as=style` is valid.

### Possible origin

#7327 added the Link header, and #7477 later added the iife/module split in `getScriptPreloadAttrs`. The `as: "script"` line in `early-hints.ts` looks like it predates the split and was not revisited when `rel` stopped always being `preload`.

### Versions

- `@tanstack/start-server-core` — reproduced in **1.167.22** (our deployed version, warnings observed in production) and the same code is present in **1.169.37**
- `@tanstack/router-core` 1.168.17 / 1.171.32
- `@tanstack/react-start` 1.167.50
- `@tanstack/react-router` 1.168.25
- Deployed on Cloudflare via Nitro

### Workaround

Stripping `as=script` from `modulepreload` entries in the `Link` response header, in our own server entry wrapper. The hint still works — it just becomes valid.

Not relevant

### Which project does this relate to?

Start

### Describe the bug

`prerender.concurrency` suggests pages are rendered in parallel, but prerendering sends every page to **one** preview server (`startPreviewServer` in `start-plugin-core/src/vite/prerender.ts`). That server runs SSR in a single JavaScript thread, so `concurrency` only overlaps I/O waits; the rendering work of each page still happens one page at a time. For sites with many CPU-bound pages, build time grows linearly with page count, and raising `concurrency` changes nothing.

This isn't adapter-specific. The reproducer uses plain Start with the default Node preview server. With `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` the preview is one workerd process running one isolate, so the effect is the same.

**Real-world impact:** in a production app with ~19k prerendered pages (CPU-bound renders from bundled static data, no network I/O), prerendering takes ~110–150s locally at `concurrency` 1, 2 or 4 alike. In CI (Cloudflare Workers Builds, 4 vCPU) the full build went from ~1 min to ~5 min once all pages were prerendered.

As an experiment I split the same pages across **4 separate preview processes** (N workerd instances started against the built `dist/server`). The output matched the built-in prerenderer's, except for the dehydration timestamp, and prerendering dropped to **~45s**, scaling with process count (1 → 2 → 4) up to the machine's performance cores. I'd rather not maintain that workaround, since it depends on internals and unstable APIs, so an official option would be great.

### Complete minimal reproducer

https://github.com/R4ULtv/tanstack-start-prerender-concurrency

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1. `git clone https://github.com/R4ULtv/tanstack-start-prerender-concurrency && cd tanstack-start-prerender-concurrency`
2. `npm install`
3. `npm run bench`. This runs `vite build` with `prerender.concurrency` set to 1, 4 and the machine's core count, and prints the time of each build. The app has one route, `/page/$id`, whose loader does ~15 ms of synchronous CPU work, with 1,000 pages prerendered (`PAGE_COUNT` to change).

Result on an Apple M-series Mac (10 logical cores, Node 24):

| concurrency | build time |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 21.3s |
| 4 | 20.4s |
| 10 | 19.6s |

### Expected behavior

With `concurrency` > 1 on a multi-core machine, prerendering CPU-bound pages should get faster. For example:

- an option such as `prerender.workers: number` that starts N preview servers (worker threads or child processes) and spreads the page queue across them; or, at least,
- documentation stating that `concurrency` only overlaps I/O and doesn't parallelize rendering.

### Screenshots or Videos

_No response_

### Platform

- Router / Start Version: @tanstack/react-start 1.168.57, @tanstack/react-router 1.170.38
- OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0), Apple M-series (4 performance + 6 efficiency cores)
- Browser: N/A (build-time issue)
- Browser Version: N/A
- Bundler: vite
- Bundler Version: 8.3.0

### Additional context

- #8430 moves the prerender preview into a Node worker, which may be a natural place to start several workers.
- Each page is requested with a trailing slash first (`/page/X/` → 307 → `/page/X`), which doubles the number of requests during prerendering. Possibly related to #7070 / #6978.
- With `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, several local workerd instances started side by side hit `SQLITE_BUSY` on the shared `.wrangler/state` until persistence was disabled per instance. That may need coordinating with the Cloudflare plugin if several preview servers are started.

body_text:
With the Rsbuild plugin, routes whose only option is `server` stay in the client route tree, so the route file is bundled for the client. The Vite plugin prunes them.

### Repro

```ts
// src/routes/api/hook.ts
import '@tanstack/react-start/server-only'
import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'

export const Route = createFileRoute('/api/hook')({
  server: { handlers: { GET: () => new Response('ok') } },
})
```

```ts
// rsbuild.config.ts and vite.config.ts
tanstackStart({ importProtection: { behavior: 'error' } })
```

Run `rsbuild build` and `vite build`.

### Expected
Both builds pass and `/api/hook` is not in the client bundle.

### Actual
Vite passes. Rsbuild fails with `[import-protection] Import denied in client environment … Importer: src/routes/api/hook.ts:1:9`, traced through `src/routeTree.gen.ts`. Without the marker it builds, but the client bundle contains an empty `createFileRoute('/api/hook')({})`.

### Possible fix
Vite gives the client a pruned tree via `clientTreePlugin` + `pruneServerOnlySubtrees` ([vite/start-router-plugin/plugin.ts#L92-L144](https://github.com/TanStack/router/blob/41ebd288677beacb8eb56953f5f8c26e9d33313e/packages/start-plugin-core/src/vite/start-router-plugin/plugin.ts#L92-L144)). [rsbuild/start-router-plugin.ts](https://github.com/TanStack/router/blob/41ebd288677beacb8eb56953f5f8c26e9d33313e/packages/start-plugin-core/src/rsbuild/start-router-plugin.ts) has no equivalent. A client-environment `api.transform` on the route tree, like the server-environment one in #8291, would cover it.

### Workaround
Move the marker into a `*.server.ts` module that the handler imports.

### Versions
@tanstack/react-start 1.168.59 (start-plugin-core 1.171.48, same on main @ 41ebd28), @rsbuild/core 2.2.10, Vite 8.3.1, Node 24.16.

### Describe the bug

After upgrading to the latest patched release of `@tanstack/react-start` (`1.168.60`, pulling in `@tanstack/start-server-core@1.169.39` and `@tanstack/router-core@1.171.34`), our app crashes on **every** SSR request to `/` when deployed to Vercel (Node.js runtime, `nodejs24.x`, nitro `vercel` preset), with:

```
TypeError: object is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))
    at handleServerRoutes (file:///var/task/_ssr/server-<hash>.mjs:1528:49)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
```

This reproduces consistently on real Vercel infrastructure (confirmed via Vercel's own runtime error/log aggregation across multiple separate deployments of the identical commit), but we have **not** been able to reproduce it by invoking the exact same built `.vercel/output/functions/__server.func/index.mjs` bundle directly in a plain Node 24 process (both `GET /` and `HEAD /` against a bare `new Request(...)` return 200 locally, full HTML). So whatever triggers it depends on something specific to the real request/runtime context Vercel provides (headers, the `context` object with a real `waitUntil`, etc.) that we haven't been able to pin down yet from the outside.

### Suspected cause

We noticed `@tanstack/start-server-core@1.169.39` was released together with #8573 ("fix(start): align server function transport behavior"), which tightened `normalizeSsrResponse`/`isSsrResponse` in `packages/router-core/src/ssr/handlerCallback.ts` to throw (`Expected a Response from the SSR handler`) instead of silently passing through non-Response values, and reshaped the server-function result contract (`result.error`/`result.result`) in `server-functions-handler.ts` and `ServerFunctionSerializationAdapter.ts`. We suspect something in our app's SSR path produces a value that no longer satisfies the new, stricter contract, and that whatever is swallowing/transforming that `TypeError` ends up presenting it as "object is not iterable" rather than the new explicit error message — but we haven't fully traced it through the minified bundle yet.

### Your Example Website or App

Not shareable (private production app), sorry — happy to provide more detail/log excerpts on request.

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue

1. Deploy a TanStack Start app to Vercel using the `vercel` nitro preset (Node.js runtime) with `@tanstack/react-start@1.168.60`.
2. Request `/` (or any SSR page) from the deployed production URL.
3. Observe a 500 with the stack trace above.

We were unable to reduce this to a minimal public repro yet since it doesn't reproduce outside real Vercel infrastructure in our testing — will update if we manage to isolate it further or narrow down which of our server functions/middleware triggers it.

SSR request to `/` should render normally, as it did on `@tanstack/react-start@1.168.26` (pre-upgrade).

_AI disclosure: Claude (Opus) investigated this and wrote this issue._

### Which project does this relate to?

Router

### Describe the bug

Follow-up to #8640, as asked in https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/8640#issuecomment-6087380304. This is only about how long loaded content waits after hydration, not about the duplicate pending component.

A `ssr: 'data-only'` / `ssr: false` route server-renders its `pendingComponent`, so the pending UI is visible from first paint. On hydration, `offerPending` starts `pendingMinMs` from now:

```ts
presentedPending ? Date.now() + min : tx[4 /* startedAt */] + delay,
```

"Now" is after the client JS has loaded. On a slow connection the pending UI has already been visible longer than the minimum, and the content still waits the full minimum again.

Not questioning the server fallback itself (#5122).

### Complete minimal reproducer

https://github.com/Tarekkharsa/tanstack-router-pending-min-after-hydration-repro

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

`pnpm i && pnpm test`: builds, serves `vite preview`, loads `/dashboard` (instant loader) in Chromium, with JS served normally and with every `/assets/*.js` held 600 ms.

### Expected behavior

Pending UI visible for at least `pendingMinMs` in total, then content as soon as code and data are ready.

### Screenshots or Videos

1.170.41, `pendingMinMs: 400`, three runs each:

| JS held | skeleton painted | code + data ready | content | wait after ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 ms | ~16 ms | ~50 ms | ~455 ms | ~405 ms |
| 600 ms | ~16 ms | ~650 ms | ~1060 ms | ~405 ms |

With `pendingMinMs: 0` the wait after ready is ~3 ms.

### Platform

- `@tanstack/react-router` 1.170.41, `@tanstack/react-start` 1.168.60
- macOS, Chromium (Playwright 1.62.1), vite 8.3.1

### Additional context

Constraint, from the reverted #8643 (#8647): in React, if the minimum has run out when `hydrate()` resolves, the load can commit `success` before React hydrates the route's Suspense boundary. The pending branch must then still render during hydration.

Tried locally, measurement only, on top of #8643 plus a hydration check in `MatchInner`:

```diff
-        presentedPending ? Date.now() + min : tx[4 /* startedAt */] + delay,
+        tx[4 /* startedAt */] + (presentedPending ? min : delay),
 ...
-    Date.now(),
+    resolvedPrefix ? Date.now() - performance.now() : Date.now(),
```

The hydration transaction then starts at navigation start. With JS held, content came ~3 ms after it was ready (12/12 loads). Caveat: navigation start is before first paint, so a fast load shows the pending UI slightly less than the minimum (~390 of 400 ms warm, ~290 ms cold).

### Which project does this relate to? Router (`@tanstack/router-plugin`, code splitting) ### Describe the bug A route option is broken when it meets both of these conditions: - it is a split target (`notFoundComponent`, `errorComponent`, …); - its value is a local identifier that another split group also uses, which makes it a *shared binding*. In that case the option's virtual module exports a name it never declares, and the bundler rejects it: ``` [PARSE_ERROR] Export 'SplitNotFoundComponent' is not defined ╭─[ src/routes/posts.$id.tsx?tsr-split=notFoundComponent:3:10 ] 3 │ export { SplitNotFoundComponent as notFoundComponent }; ``` It happens only when the install holds **two copies of `@babel/traverse`**, which pnpm produces easily: - `babel-dead-code-elimination` (pulled in by `@tanstack/router-utils`) resolves one copy; - `@babel/core` resolves another. Our lockfile reached that state from a plain `pnpm up` of the TanStack Start packages: `@babel/core@7.29.7 → @babel/traverse@7.29.8`, and `babel-dead-code-elimination@1.0.12 → @babel/traverse@7.29.10`. ### Minimal route ```tsx import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router' export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts/$id')({ component: PostRoute, notFoundComponent: PostNotFound, }) function PostNotFound() { return

Not found

} function PostRoute() { const post = usePost() if (!post) return return

{post.title}

} declare function usePost(): { title: string } | undefined ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. `package.json`: ```json { "private": true, "dependencies": { "@tanstack/router-plugin": "1.168.46", "@tanstack/react-router": "1.170.44", "react": "19.2.8", "react-dom": "19.2.8" } } ``` 2. `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, to get the two-copy layout on purpose: ```yaml packages: [] overrides: "@babel/core>@babel/traverse": 7.29.8 ``` 3. `pnpm install`. Then either run a Vite build with the router plugin and `autoCodeSplitting`, or call the compiler directly: ```js import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs' import { computeSharedBindings, compileCodeSplitVirtualRoute } from './node_modules/@tanstack/router-plugin/dist/esm/core/code-splitter/compilers.js' const filename = 'route.tsx' const code = readFileSync(filename, 'utf8') const codeSplitGroupings = [['component'], ['errorComponent'], ['notFoundComponent']] const sharedBindings = computeSharedBindings({ code, filename, codeSplitGroupings }) console.log(sharedBindings) // Set { 'PostNotFound' } console.log(compileCodeSplitVirtualRoute({ code, filename, splitTargets: ['notFoundComponent'], sharedBindings }).code) ``` ### Actual ```js import { PostNotFound } from "route.tsx?tsr-shared=1"; export { SplitNotFoundComponent as notFoundComponent }; ``` ### Expected What the same code produces with a single `@babel/traverse` copy: ```js import { PostNotFound } from "route.tsx?tsr-shared=1"; export { PostNotFound as notFoundComponent }; ``` ### Cause In `compileCodeSplitVirtualRoute`: 1. `findReferencedIdentifiers(ast)` (router-utils → `babel-dead-code-elimination` → traverse copy **A**) traverses the program and caches its scope, including the `PostNotFound` binding. 2. `removeSharedDeclarations(ast, sharedBindings)` filters `ast.program.body` directly. `PostNotFound`'s declaration is gone, but no scope is updated. 3. `babel.traverse(ast, …)` (`@babel/core` → traverse copy **B**) resolves the split node with `programPath.scope.getBinding('PostNotFound')`. - **One copy:** B reuses the scope A cached in step 1 and gets the *stale* binding to the removed `FunctionDeclaration`. The `isFunctionDeclaration` branch sets `localExporterIdent = 'PostNotFound'`, which the shared import added later happens to satisfy. It works only because of the stale cache. - **Two copies:** B crawls fresh, the declaration is already gone, and `getBinding` returns `undefined`. `splitNode` is `undefined`, so no `const SplitNotFoundComponent = …` is ever emitted, but the export is still written. To prove it with a single copy, add `babel.traverse.cache.clear()` right after `removeSharedDeclarations(...)`. The single-copy install then fails exactly like the two-copy one. ### Scope - Reproduced on `@tanstack/router-plugin` 1.168.46 and 1.168.35, so it is not a recent regression. - `errorComponent` breaks the same way (`SplitErrorComponent`). I expect any split key whose value is a shared identifier to be affected. ### Possible fixes - When a split target's identifier is in `sharedBindings`, export it straight from the shared import (`localExporterIdent = originalIdentName`) instead of resolving it through a scope that step 2 made stale. - Or resolve split nodes before `removeSharedDeclarations` mutates the body. - Separately: router-utils and `babel-dead-code-elimination` using a different `@babel/traverse` instance from `@babel/core` makes any cross-pass scope reuse depend on how the package manager dedupes. ### Workarounds - Wrap the option in an arrow, `notFoundComponent: () => `. The split node is then an arrow expression and no binding lookup happens. - Or dedupe `@babel/traverse` to a single copy. That only brings back the stale-cache behaviour that happens to work. ### Your environment - `@tanstack/router-plugin` 1.168.46 (also 1.168.35), `@tanstack/router-utils` 1.162.4, `babel-dead-code-elimination` 1.0.12 - `@babel/core` 7.29.7, `@babel/traverse` 7.29.8 + 7.29.10 - pnpm 10.24.0, Vite 8.2.2 (rolldown), Node 22.23.3 - Found through `@tanstack/react-start` 1.169.2

body_text:
### Describe the bug

With `defaultViewTransition: true`, `router.startViewTransition` (`router-core/src/router.ts`) calls
`document.startViewTransition(fn).updateCallbackDone` and drops the `ViewTransition` object.
Its `ready` and `finished` promises get no handler.

`updateCallbackDone` settles when the DOM update is done, well before the animation ends. So any
navigation that starts while the previous cross-fade is still animating skips that transition,
the browser rejects its `ready` with `AbortError: Transition was skipped. New ViewTransition started`,
and nothing handles the rejection. `await router.navigate()` does not prevent it, because it
resolves on `updateCallbackDone`.

In an app this is console noise on quick consecutive navigations. In a test runner
(vitest browser mode) it fails the whole run: every test passes, then vitest reports
"Unhandled Rejection" and exits non-zero.

### Reproduction

Vitest browser mode (chromium), no UI needed:

```ts
import { createMemoryHistory, createRootRoute, createRoute, createRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'
import { test } from 'vitest'

test('two navigations in a row', async () => {
  const root = createRootRoute()
  const a = createRoute({ getParentRoute: () => root, path: '/a' })
  const b = createRoute({ getParentRoute: () => root, path: '/b' })
  const router = createRouter({
    routeTree: root.addChildren([a, b]),
    history: createMemoryHistory({ initialEntries: ['/a'] }),
    defaultViewTransition: true,
  })
  await router.load()
  await router.navigate({ to: '/b' })
  await router.navigate({ to: '/a' })
})
```

### Which project does this relate to?

Start (`@tanstack/react-start`, deferred hydration / `<Hydrate>`)

### Describe the bug

A `<Hydrate>` boundary (e.g. `when={visible()}`) loses its server-rendered HTML during initial hydration whenever **any context provider above it changes its value** before the gate opens. The boundary ends up empty (its `fallback`, `null` by default) until the strategy fires (e.g. until the user scrolls to it).

This happens in practice in almost any real app, because root providers commonly update right after mount (session probe setting `isLogged`, attribution/analytics state, a provider that publishes `value={{ ... }}` and re-renders on router changes, etc.).

The deferred-hydration guide says:

> React may hydrate a deferred boundary earlier than its strategy would normally allow if state, props, context, or store updates outside the boundary require React to reconcile inside it before the gate opens. This preserves correctness and avoids showing stale server HTML after the surrounding app has changed.

React does try to do that, but the early hydration can never succeed, because `HydrationBoundary` keeps throwing the gate promise until the strategy resolves:

```tsx
// packages/react-start-client/src/hydration/visible.tsx (same shape in the other strategies)
function HydrationBoundary(props) {
  const { g, o } = props
  if (!g.r) {
    if (!reactUse) throw g.p
    reactUse(g.p)
  }
  ...
}
```

What React 19.3 does (react-dom-client):
1. `propagateContextChanges` reaches the dehydrated fragment (fiber tag 18). It cannot know whether there are consumers inside, so it schedules work on the parent Suspense boundary.
2. `updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent` sees the update and attempts hydration at a bumped lane (`SelectiveHydrationException`).
3. That attempt suspends again on the closed gate. On the retry lane React calls `renderDidSuspendDelayIfPossible()` and `retrySuspenseComponentWithoutHydrating(...)`. For non-transition updates this commits a client render: the server HTML is deleted and the fallback is shown.

So the correctness promise in the guide doesn't hold: instead of hydrating early, the boundary switches to client rendering and shows nothing until the gate opens.

### Your Example Website or App

Minimal shape (no router needed to reproduce the React side):

```tsx
const Ctx = createContext(0)
function Provider({ children }) {
  const [n, setN] = useState(0)
  useEffect(() => setN(1), []) // any value change after mount
  return <Ctx.Provider value={n}>{children}</Ctx.Provider>
}

<Provider>
  <Header />
  {/* tall content so the boundary is below the fold */}
  <Hydrate when={visible()}>
    <Footer /> {/* does not even read Ctx */}
  </Hydrate>
</Provider>
```

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue

1. Production build (`vite build`) with a `<Hydrate when={visible()}>` boundary below the fold, under a provider whose value changes in a mount effect.
2. Load the page and do not scroll.
3. Check the DOM shortly after hydration. The boundary's server HTML is gone; a `MutationObserver` shows it removed in the same commit as the provider update. Scroll down: the content renders again on the client.

Hoisting the `<Hydrate>` element to a module constant, so it never gets new props, doesn't help: the trigger is context propagation, not props.

### Expected behavior

Either:
- the gate opens when React asks to hydrate the boundary early, which is what the guide describes; or
- the docs state that `<Hydrate>` only keeps its SSR HTML if no context above it changes before the gate opens.

### Platform

- `@tanstack/react-start` 1.169.2 (`react-start-client` 1.168.42; `visible.tsx` is unchanged on `main`)
- `react` / `react-dom` 19.3.1
- Chromium (Playwright), production build served by Nitro

### Additional context

We are working around it by moving the state of our root providers into external stores read with `useSyncExternalStore`, so their context value never changes after mount. The guide does not hint at this, and any third-party provider that updates on mount would still break it.

**Versions:** - @tanstack/react-router 1.170.18 - @tanstack/router-core 1.171.15 - @tanstack/react-start 1.167.x (start-client-core 1.170.14) - React 19.2 - Vite 8.1, dev mode ## Describe the bug A full page load of a URL under an `ssr: false` layout, where a child route's async `beforeLoad` throws `redirect()`, can leave the page blank. The console shows `Uncaught undefined` and "An error occurred in the component". Navigating to the same URL client-side works. This is the issue reported in #7910, which was closed for lack of a reproducer. Here is one with no `.preload()` forwarding. ## Minimal reproduction ```tsx // routes/zzrepro.tsx export const Route = createFileRoute("/zzrepro")({ ssr: false, beforeLoad: async () => { await wait(200); return { user: { id: "x" } } }, component: () => , }) // routes/zzrepro.a.tsx export const Route = createFileRoute("/zzrepro/a")({ beforeLoad: async () => { await wait(200); throw redirect({ to: "/zzrepro/b" }) }, component: () =>
A
, }) // routes/zzrepro.b.tsx export const Route = createFileRoute("/zzrepro/b")({ beforeLoad: async () => { await wait(200) }, component: () =>
B rendered OK
, }) ``` In our app, the redirect alone was enough to blank the page. In this synthetic version it reproduces deterministically if `router.invalidate()` is also called while the redirected load is in flight, about 500–900 ms after page load. For example, Supabase's `onAuthStateChange` emits `SIGNED_IN` on every page load. A root-level listener that calls `router.invalidate()` on it hits this window. ## Analysis 1. The `ssr: false` match is dehydrated as `pending`. On the client, `hydrate()` puts it in the active matches, and `router.load()` runs the guards. 2. The child throws a redirect. `navigate({ replace: true })` starts a new load whose pending matches reuse the same id for the `ssr: false` layout. They share `_nonReactive`. 3. That load finishes the layout match. `loadRouteMatch` resolves and clears `_nonReactive.loadPromise`. This happens before `onReady` commits the pending matches. 4. React renders the still-active stale snapshot (`status: "pending"`). `MatchInnerImpl` does `throw getMatchPromise(match, "loadPromise")`, which is `undefined`. 5. `CatchBoundary` stores `undefined` as the error. That is falsy, so it re-renders its children, which throw again. React gives up and unmounts the root. 6. The router state afterwards is correct (all matches `success`), but nothing is mounted. `router.state.status` stays `pending` forever. ## Workaround we ship (patch-package) In `MatchInnerImpl`'s `getMatchPromise`: ```js return router.getMatch(match.id)?._nonReactive[key] ?? match._nonReactive[key] ?? router.latestLoadPromise ?? new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0)) ``` ## Suggested fixes - Never throw a non-thenable from the pending branches. - Or keep `loadPromise` alive until the pending matches are committed. - Separately, `CatchBoundary` could treat a thrown `undefined` as an error, so it renders the `errorComponent` instead of looping.

B rendered OK

### TanStack Table version

9.1.2

### Framework/Library version

React 19.2.8

### Describe the bug and the steps to reproduce it

Tanstack table uses internally mutable state, something that goes against Reacts immutability assumptions. This creates issues with the react compiler. v9 tries to make it work with the compiler by making the table object a non stable object. This happens to work out in many cases, not because it now follows the rules of react but because exactly how the compiler currently reason about those rules often shake out that way. Depending on internal implementation details like this and advocating for your users to leave the compiler on for components using tanstack table seem irresponsible as a future version of the compiler could suddenly break your users apps. 

The attached stackblitz shows how sending a value to a completely unrelated hook can cause react compiler to make different decisions, breaking something that previously worked out. To me this demonstrates that what tanstack table is doing is still fundamentally breaking the react compilers rules and could break at any time.

This is causing issues with Octane as well as it wants to rely on similar assumptions as the react compiler for its optimizations. That is probably not your issue to solve but mentioning it as well as it was through investigating weird decisions around memoization in Octane that I discovered this issue. https://github.com/octanejs/octane/issues/846#issuecomment-5432084415

### TanStack Table version

v9.2.4

### Framework/Library version

React 19.3.0

### Describe the bug and the steps to reproduce it

The [documentation](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/guide/data#give-data-a-stable-reference) mentions that in v9 the `data` is an atom which is not reactive from my understanding. A common scenario in many applications is extracting components for header, body, footer, even the whole table to have a single component to style and manage. 

Especially with React Compiler enabled, I noticed that many reusable components via `createTableHook` were not rerendering, although I could see state updates in the devtools. The documentation explains this behaviour [here](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/react-compiler#choose-the-narrowest-subscription-that-stays-correct), suggesting the following:

>If a component depends on several state slices, subscribe to table.store and return all of those slices from the selector. Keep the state-dependent Table calls inside the Subscribe render function: 
>
>The selector must include every state slice that can change the result of table.getRowModel() for this table. That may include filtering, sorting, grouping, expansion, or pagination, depending on the features in use.

While I can use `table.Subscribe` to select the table feature states, I haven't found a way to subscribe to `data` changes other than to pass the whole `data` with prop drilling to sync data changes with consumer components (I still won't use the data, I will use row models, but at least this ensures row model consumers will be rerendered when data changes). There is an [example](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/react-compiler#choose-the-narrowest-subscription-that-stays-correct) that shows a reusable `TableBody` component, but this has the same issue: if data changes and table subscribed states are not the reason why (see scenarios below), the component will not rerender and stale data will be shown until a pagination, filter, sorting or any other subscribed feature state is updated. 

There are several valid scenarios where this may be needed, cases where `data` may be externally updated and the `table` needs to rerender to show the latest state, such as:

- if `data` is a React state, calling setState
- using Tanstack Query, there is `polling`, `refetchOnWindowFocus` or infinite query scroll event listeners
- Websocket updates

In the sandbox you will find 2 tables and the realtime data from the state which I update every 2 seconds:

- `table1` is based on a datatable component extracted via `createTableHook`, similar to v8 style reusable table components. While the documentation says that the changes in `data` will cause the row models to be regenerated, the `table` object itself is a stable reference which has not changed (feature states have not changed), so although `table.getRowModel()` returns different, new data, the `table` object doesn't trigger a rerender to reflect that since no subscribed state has been updated.

- `table2` is comes from an example from the documetation where the table reusable components are consumed in the same component where the `data` and `table` live (`App` in this case). While the `table` rows update, I think this example is misleading in the documentation as the nested components are updated because the `App` component rerenders due to `setData` rather than the Tanstack Table internal signals. If I were to have a new component in between, so `App` consumes `NewComponent` which consumes `DatatableBody`, the table rows will not be rerendered just like in table1. 

This behaviour theoretically could apply to any table option change as well (because they are not states), I don't know if this may be an issue or not for some users, just stating what I found. Also, while this behaviour is more evident in apps with React Compiler enabled due to a potential case of internal mutability, the same behaviour should happen without the compiler as well with manual memoization. The only difference is that without the compiler, by default if the `data` changes, it will be in the same or a higher component than the table components, so every component below will be rerendered, masking this issue. 

I hope it's a valid issue and not me not understanding how to new state management works under the hood, wasting your time :(

What is the best way to handle this scenario where I want to have table data that may be updated externally? 
What is the correct way to defined reusable components via `createTableHook` that are reactive to the row model changes? Are there any examples? 

PS: Fantastic job on the v9 update btw, apart from this, I have been really enjoying it and the codebase looks cleaner than ever. 

### Your Minimal, Reproducible Example - (Sandbox Highly Recommended)

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-eyxvcbv9?file=src%2Fmain.tsx

### Screenshots or Videos (Optional)

_No response_

None

### Describe the problem

I'm currently migrating from Electron to Tauri, but I've found that Tauri doesn't have a method like Electron's BrowserWindow.setOpacity to set the transparency of the entire window. It can only be achieved by setting the transparency of the web page through CSS. However, this doesn't meet my requirements because my application loads external web pages whose CSS I can't control. Therefore, I hope there could be a way similar to BrowserWindow.setOpacity to set the window's transparency.

### Describe the solution you'd like

### Describe the problem

Starting from version 0.16.0, rpm-rs provides a feature flag (`zstdmt`) that can be used to enable multithreaded zstd compression (https://github.com/rpm-rs/rpm/pull/239).

https://github.com/rpm-rs/rpm/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#0160

tauri-bundler already uses rpm-rs v0.16, but this feature flag is not currently enabled.

https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/a03219ca196372fca542633900a5ad26d805fcf7/crates/tauri-bundler/Cargo.toml#L68


### Describe the solution you'd like

I think that supporting multithreaded compression could significantly improve RPM build performance, especially after switching from the default gzip compression to zstd.

https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/a03219ca196372fca542633900a5ad26d805fcf7/crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/rpm.rs#L64-L76

However, multithreaded compression probably shouldn't be enabled by default, since it can affect existing build environments to some extent.

It may be more appropriate to expose it as a configurable option when using zstd compression, and keep it disabled by default.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

body_text:
### Describe the bug

I am planning to use Tauri to develop a new iOS application and want to integrate a third-party SDK to implement a certain feature.

After configuring the SDK in Package.swift, I imported the SDK in the plugin and started development.

Running cargo build compiles successfully, but running cargo build --target aarch64-apple-ios fails.

The error says the module cannot be found.

I tested several dependencies, and currently, [Google Mobile Ads](https://github.com/googleads/swift-package-manager-google-mobile-ads) and [OneSignal iOS SDK](https://github.com/OneSignal/OneSignal-iOS-SDK)
 consistently report the module not found error.

When examining their Package.swift, I noticed that they both have a binaryTarget whose name is the same as the package name.

For example, Google Mobile Ads:

```swift
// ...
let package = Package(
  name: "GoogleMobileAds",
  platforms: [.iOS(.v12)],
  products: [
    .library(
      name: "GoogleMobileAds",
      targets: ["GoogleMobileAdsTarget"]
    )
  ],
  // ...
  targets: [
    // ...
    .binaryTarget(
      name: "GoogleMobileAds",
      url:
        "https://dl.google.com/googleadmobadssdk/c8c5523373ed76aa/googlemobileadsios-spm-12.14.0.zip",
      checksum: "c8c5523373ed76aa6da7bbe1324458e680981bd4593271cca5958fc8e8ffc5e7"
    ),
  ]
)
```

My Code:

```swift
import FirebaseAnalytics
import OneSignalFramework
import GoogleMobileAds
import SwiftRs
import Tauri
import UIKit
import WebKit

class PingArgs: Decodable {
  let value: String?
}

class ExamplePlugin: Plugin {
  @objc public func ping(_ invoke: Invoke) throws {
    let args = try invoke.parseArgs(PingArgs.self)
    invoke.resolve(["value": args.value ?? ""])
  }
}

@_cdecl("init_plugin_my_plugin_copy")
func initPlugin() -> Plugin {
  return ExamplePlugin()
}
```

Related issues: #13332, #14504


### Reproduction

1. npx @tauri-apps/cli plugin new my-plugin --ios
2. edit `tauri-plugin-my-plugin/ios/Package.swift`

    ```swift
    import PackageDescription
    
    let package = Package(
      name: "tauri-plugin-my-plugin-copy",
      platforms: [
        .macOS(.v10_13),
        .iOS(.v13),
      ],
      products: [
        // Products define the executables and libraries a package produces, and make them visible to other packages.
        .library(
          name: "tauri-plugin-my-plugin-copy",
          type: .static,
          targets: ["tauri-plugin-my-plugin-copy"])
      ],
      dependencies: [
        .package(name: "Tauri", path: "../.tauri/tauri-api"),
        .package(
          name: "Firebase", url: "https://github.com/firebase/firebase-ios-sdk",
          from: "8.15.0"),
        .package(
          name: "OneSignalFramework", url: "https://github.com/OneSignal/OneSignal-iOS-SDK",
          .upToNextMajor(from: "5.2.15")),
        .package(
          name: "GMAds",
          url: "https://github.com/googleads/swift-package-manager-google-mobile-ads", from: "12.14.0"),
      ],
      targets: [
        // Targets are the basic building blocks of a package. A target can define a module or a test suite.
        // Targets can depend on other targets in this package, and on products in packages this package depends on.
        .target(
          name: "tauri-plugin-my-plugin-copy",
          dependencies: [
            .byName(name: "Tauri"),
            .product(name: "FirebaseAnalytics", package: "Firebase"),
            .product(name: "OneSignalFramework", package: "OneSignalFramework"),
            .product(name: "GoogleMobileAds", package: "GMAds"),
          ],
          path: "Sources")
      ]
    )
    ```

        invoke.resolve(["value": args.value ?? ""])

can found module.

## Describe the bug When running `tauri dev`, the WebView intermittently shows the default "Welcome to Tauri + React" template that's embedded in the CLI binary instead of loading content from the configured `devUrl` (http://localhost:1420). ### What's happening: - The Vite dev server IS running correctly on port 1420 and serving the correct content (verified with `curl http://localhost:1420/src/App.tsx` which returns the correct transpiled code) - The Rust backend IS working correctly (logs show it initializing, finding files, etc.) - The WebView just doesn't load from devUrl - it shows the fallback template instead - Even `Cmd+R` to refresh doesn't fix it - the fallback template persists ### Key finding: The default template HTML is embedded directly in the CLI binary: ```bash strings node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli-darwin-arm64/cli.darwin-arm64.node | grep "Welcome to Tauri" # Returns:

Welcome to Tauri!

``` This suggests the WebView is loading a fallback/placeholder instead of connecting to devUrl. ## Reproduction 1. Create a Tauri v2 app with React + Vite 2. Run `bun run tauri dev` (or npm/pnpm equivalent) 3. Intermittently, the window shows "Welcome to Tauri + React" default template instead of the actual app 4. The issue persists even after waiting 30+ seconds 5. `Cmd+R` refresh does not fix it 6. Killing all processes and restarting sometimes fixes it, sometimes doesn't **Reproduction rate:** ~50% of the time in my testing. No clear pattern identified (tried tmux vs foreground, different wait times, etc.) ## Expected behavior The WebView should always load content from the configured `devUrl` when the dev server is running and accessible. ## Full `tauri info` output ``` tauri-cli: 2.9.6 tauri (rust crate): 2.9.5 ``` ## Stack trace No crash - the app runs but shows wrong content. ## Additional context **Environment:** - macOS: 26.1 (Build 25B78) - macOS Tahoe - Architecture: darwin-arm64 (Apple Silicon) - Bun: 1.3.5 - Vite: 7.3.1 - Node: 22.20.0 **tauri.conf.json:** ```json { "$schema": "https://schema.tauri.app/config/2", "productName": "diff-ai", "version": "0.1.0", "identifier": "com.luisrudge.diff-ai", "build": { "beforeDevCommand": "bun run dev", "devUrl": "http://localhost:1420", "beforeBuildCommand": "bun run build", "frontendDist": "../dist" }, "app": { "windows": [ { "title": "diff-ai", "width": 1200, "height": 800, "maximized": true } ], "security": { "csp": null } } } ``` **Screenshot of the bug:** The WebView shows this default template instead of my actual React app: ![Welcome to Tauri + React default template with Tauri, Vite, and React logos, "Enter a name" input field and "Greet" button] (The actual app should show a diff viewer UI with file tree, not this default template)

body_text: ### Describe the bug Browsers can create "pictureInPicture" child windows for the current webpage that allow some part of the content to exist outside of the current browser tab. Google does this when you're in a meeting for example, and you switch to a different tab. This functionality has been supported on modern browser for a while and recently, Tauri tightened security around these windows (see #14411 for reference) but still allows windows to be created through the Rust "backend". Creating such a PictureInPicture window requires that the child window has a `window.location.href` of `about:blank`. Setting any other URL there causes the window to be closed automatically. Any content in this window will be created and controlled from the parent window instance, via Javascript. This causes a problem when the parent window tries to add HTML code that needs to load some kind of static asset, like an image. The webview will try to load this image via a regular HTTP request to http://tauri.localhost, but since it's coming from `about:blank`, it will be missing a Referer header / Origin. Tauri will outright refuse serving any local assets to requests without a Referer and immediately terminate the request with a "connection refused". ### Reproduction ```js const child = await window.documentPictureInPicture.requestWindow(); child.document.body.innerHTML = ""; ``` ### Expected behavior The `image.png` file is loaded properly. ### Full `tauri info` output ```text > botc-app@3.50.1 tauri > tauri info [✔] Environment - OS: Solus 4.8.0 x86_64 (X64) (budgie-desktop on x11) ✔ webkit2gtk-4.1: 2.50.4 ✔ rsvg2: 2.61.1 ✔ rustc: 1.85.0 (4d91de4e4 2025-02-17) ✔ cargo: 1.85.0 (d73d2caf9 2024-12-31) ✔ rustup: 1.28.1 (f9edccde0 2025-03-05) ✔ Rust toolchain: stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (default) - node: 24.0.1 - npm: 11.3.0 - deno: deno 2.6.6 [-] Packages - tauri 🦀: 2.9.2, (outdated, latest: 2.9.5) - tauri-build 🦀: 2.5.1, (outdated, latest: 2.5.3) - wry 🦀: 0.53.5, (outdated, latest: 0.54.1) - tao 🦀: 0.34.5 - @tauri-apps/api ⱼₛ: 2.9.0 (outdated, latest: 2.9.1) - @tauri-apps/cli ⱼₛ: 2.9.2 (outdated, latest: 2.9.6) [-] Plugins - tauri-plugin-dialog 🦀: 2.4.2, (outdated, latest: 2.6.0) - @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog ⱼₛ: 2.4.2 (outdated, latest: 2.6.0) - tauri-plugin-os 🦀: 2.3.2 - @tauri-apps/plugin-os ⱼₛ: 2.3.2 - tauri-plugin-shell 🦀: 2.3.3, (outdated, latest: 2.3.4) - @tauri-apps/plugin-shell ⱼₛ: not installed! - tauri-plugin-window-state 🦀: 2.4.1 - @tauri-apps/plugin-window-state ⱼₛ: 2.4.1 - tauri-plugin-process 🦀: 2.3.1 - @tauri-apps/plugin-process ⱼₛ: 2.3.1 - tauri-plugin-updater 🦀: 2.9.0 - @tauri-apps/plugin-updater ⱼₛ: 2.9.0 - tauri-plugin-fs 🦀: 2.4.4, (outdated, latest: 2.4.5) - @tauri-apps/plugin-fs ⱼₛ: 2.4.4 (outdated, latest: 2.4.5) [-] App - build-type: bundle - CSP: unset - frontendDist: ../dist - devUrl: http://localhost:8080/ - framework: Vue.js - bundler: Vite ``` ### Stack trace ```text Failed to load resource: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED ``` ### Additional context It would be great if there was an easy config override for allow empty referers on static asset requests.

Google does this when you're in a meeting for example, and you switch to a different tab. This functionality has been supported on modern browser for a while and recently, Tauri tightened security around these windows (see #14411 for reference) but still allows windows to be created through the Rust "backend". Creating such a PictureInPicture window requires that the child window has a `window.location.href` of `about:blank`. Setting any other URL there causes the window to be closed automatically. Any content in this window will be created and controlled from the parent window instance, via Javascript. This causes a problem when the parent window tries to add HTML code that needs to load some kind of static asset, like an image. The webview will try to load this image via a regular HTTP request to http://tauri.localhost, but since it's coming from `about:blank`, it will be missing a Referer header / Origin. ### Describe the problem

I can vendor everything, but when I build from linux for windows, `nsis_tauri_utils.dll` is downloaded during the bundling process. It would be nice to be able to add the file to the repository so  I can bundle a windows release without any internet.

This is a hard requirement to make medical software as I need to be able to build without changing anything/without downloading anything. A Linux build is possible with a docker image and my repository with vendored dependencies.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Be able to download and store the file and configure in tauri.conf.json where it is located so that it is not downloaded during bundling.

### Alternatives considered

> This issue has been upstreamed from https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/issues/3702 

When checking https://tauri.app/release/ both the left-side column or by forcing manually the URL, we can see that 1.x versions stops at 1.6.0. However, there were quite some other releases since then (latest currently is 1.8.3)

Sure, there's a 1.x website at https://v1.tauri.app/releases/ where every releases are, but there are 0.x and 1.x releases on the main (v2) one, leading to user failing to grasp while these version are here up to 1.6.0 and not anymore after this. If the choice was to not add 1.x versions on the v2 website anymore, then maybe it'd be less confusing to remove every 0.x and 1.x release from there and only have a generic link sending to the v1 website on the releases pages.

### Describe the bug

I am the maintainer of a Tauri v2 application [(Windows 11 Clipboard History)](https://github.com/gustavosett/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux). I am receiving consistent reports from users on Nvidia GPUs(Fedora 43, Arch/CachyOS, Zorin OS 18) where the application crashes on launch or renders incorrectly.

The issue is strictly triggered by the "transparent": true window configuration in tauri.conf.json.

Symptoms:

Crash on Launch: Users report Error 71 (Protocol error) or Failed to create GBM buffer.

Broken Rendering (with workarounds): Attempting to force software rendering or disable explicit sync allows the app to open, but breaks transparency (black corners) or causes severe visual artifacts ("ghost" pages/tabs remaining visible underneath the current view).

This appears to be a conflict between WebKitGTK's DMABUF renderer and Nvidia's driver when handling transparent surfaces.

### Reproduction

1. Environment: Linux (Fedora 43 / Arch), Nvidia GPU (40xx/50xx series), Proprietary Drivers (v590+).
2. Repository: https://github.com/gustavosett/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux
3. Config: Ensure tauri.conf.json has "transparent": true and "decorations": false.
4. Run: npm run tauri dev (or build the bundle).

Observed: The app immediately crashes with the stack trace below.

### Expected behavior

The window should launch with transparency enabled and rounded corners, without crashing or requiring environment variable workarounds that degrade performance/visuals (as it does on Intel/AMD GPUs).

### Full `tauri info` output

```text
    ~/Doc/r/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux    master !1  npm run tauri info        ✔ 

> win11-clipboard-history@0.5.2 tauri
> tauri info


[✔] Environment
    - OS: Manjaro 26.0.2 x86_64 (X64) (xfce on x11)
    ✔ webkit2gtk-4.1: 2.50.4
    ✔ rsvg2: 2.61.3
    ✔ rustc: 1.93.0 (254b59607 2026-01-19)
    ✔ cargo: 1.93.0 (083ac5135 2025-12-15)
    ✔ rustup: 1.28.2 (e4f3ad6f8 2025-04-28)
    ✔ Rust toolchain: stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (default)
    - node: 24.13.0
    - npm: 11.6.2

[-] Packages
    - tauri 🦀: 2.10.2
    - tauri-build 🦀: 2.5.5
    - wry 🦀: 0.54.1
    - tao 🦀: 0.34.5
    - @tauri-apps/api  ⱼₛ: 2.10.1
    - @tauri-apps/cli  ⱼₛ: 2.10.0

[-] Plugins
    - tauri-plugin-global-shortcut 🦀: 2.3.1
    - @tauri-apps/plugin-global-shortcut  ⱼₛ: 2.3.1
    - tauri-plugin-single-instance 🦀: 2.4.0
    - @tauri-apps/plugin-single-instance  ⱼₛ: not installed!
    - tauri-plugin-shell 🦀: 2.3.5
    - @tauri-apps/plugin-shell  ⱼₛ: 2.3.5

[-] App
    - build-type: bundle
    - CSP: unset
    - frontendDist: ../dist
    - devUrl: http://localhost:1420/
    - framework: React
    - bundler: Vite
```

### Stack trace

```text
[Session] Detected Wayland via XDG_SESSION_TYPE
(win11-clipboard-history-bin:22857): libayatana-appindicator-WARNING **: libayatana-appindicator is deprecated.

Failed to create GBM buffer of size 360x480: Das Argument ist ungültig
[ThemeManager] Portal query failed: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)

Gdk-Message: Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display.
```

### Additional context

We have attempted standard WebKit environment variables to bypass the GBM crash. While some flags allow the window to spawn, **none result in a usable application**.

**Analysis of Workarounds:**

| Flag Attempted | Result | Visual Defects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Default (No Flags)** | **CRASH** | `Error 71 (Protocol error)` or `GBM buffer invalid argument`. |
| `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` | **Broken Visuals** | **Transparency fails completely.** Rounded corners become solid black squares. Performance is significantly degraded. |
| `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` | **Artifacts** | **Ghosting.** Previous views/tabs remain visible underneath the current view ("Ghost Pages"). Glitches only clear when the mouse hovers over them. |
| `GSK_RENDERER=gl` / `cairo` | **Unstable** | Often results in the same ghosting artifacts described above or crashes. |

**References:**

* Relevant Issue in my repo: [https://github.com/gustavosett/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux/issues/93](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/gustavosett/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux/issues/93)
* Relevant Issue in my repo: [https://github.com/gustavosett/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux/issues/120](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/gustavosett/Windows-11-Clipboard-History-For-Linux/issues/120)

### Describe the problem

I use Void Linux. Since XBPS has a limited selection of apps, unless I want to use Flatpak or AppImages then I basically just have to build things from source. I've got quite used to this.

Usually this looks like the classic `./configure; make; make install`, or some variant thereof.

Today I was installing Martichou/rquickshare, which is made using Tauri. And I realised that Tauri doesn't seem to have an equivalent of `make install`.

Of course, this was easy to work around. I just had to `sudo cp ./src-tauri/target/release/rquickshare /usr/bin/` and `sudo cp ./src-tauri/target/release/bundle/rpm/rquickshare-0.11.5-1.x86_64/usr/share/applications/rquickshare.destop /usr/share/applications/`. But it would be convenient if the Tauri CLI provided a helper command for this.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I'd like to see the ability to run `tauri install` to install the application on the current system.

### Describe the bug

when running a cef app with transparent:true
I get these errors:
```
[7542:7542:0715/104252.353262:ERROR:content/browser/gpu/gpu_process_host.cc:1089] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=139
[7542:7542:0715/104256.038834:ERROR:content/browser/gpu/gpu_process_host.cc:1089] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=139
[7542:7542:0715/104259.525112:ERROR:content/browser/gpu/gpu_process_host.cc:1089] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=139
[8363:8372:0715/104259.543699:ERROR:ui/base/x/x11_software_bitmap_presenter.cc:147] XGetWindowAttributes failed for window 52428804
```

If i pass --disable-gpu I still get:
```
[8363:8372:0715/104259.543699:ERROR:ui/base/x/x11_software_bitmap_presenter.cc:147] XGetWindowAttributes failed for window 52428804
```

in both cases, a constant black screen stays.

### temp fix
setting transparent:false has it working with no errors

### Reproduction

Set transparent: true and run cef app

### Expected behavior

Transparency works
and the app not crashing/staying black

### Describe the problem On Windows there is no supported point at which an application can act on its own window between `CreateWindowExW` and the moment the window first appears on screen. `WebviewWindowBuilder::build()` creates the HWND, applies the requested state, shows the window, and only then hands back a `WebviewWindow`. Every hook Tauri does expose - `RunEvent::WindowEvent`, `on_window_event`, the returned handle - is reached after the window has already been shown at least once. Some launch-time details I needed to apply have to land before the first frame, and none of them can be expressed on the builder. Currently I must resort to using `SetWindowsHookExW`.
The things I need

Just mentioning for completeness what I encountered: 1. **Exact placement in physical pixels.** The builder only takes logical coordinates. tao resolves those to a monitor with a search of its own - the first monitor on which the position, scaled by *that* monitor's factor, lands. On a mixed-DPI setup that can be a different monitor than the position was derived from, and for a window remembered half off an edge it can be no monitor at all, which falls back to the default cascade position. A window restoring its saved geometry therefore opens in the wrong place. A rectangle in physical pixels has no such ambiguity, but there is no way to pass one. 2. **The caption/taskbar icon.** tao gives the window a single icon - the largest image decoded out of `icon.ico` - which Windows then squeezes into the ~16px caption slot, so the small icon is a badly downscaled 256x256. Applying proper `WM_SETICON` `ICON_SMALL`/`ICON_BIG` images after `build()` returns means the frame and the taskbar button have already been drawn with tao's. 3. **Activation.** We must build with `.focused(false)`: wry calls `MoveFocus` as the last step of a focused webview build and propagates the result. But Tauri passes that same flag to the window, so tao shows it with `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` and the launch never comes to the foreground. There is no way to say "show the window activated, but do not move focus into the webview": one flag controls both. 4. **`maximized: true`.** As observed with tao 0.35, a window asked to open maximized is maximized while hidden, then shown with `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` - which carries `SW_SHOWNORMAL`'s "most recent size and position" meaning and therefore *restores* it - and only then maximized again. What the user sees is the window arriving at its restored size and being animated up to fill the screen on every single launch.

### Describe the solution you'd like A creation-time escape hatch on the window builder, plus (ideally) fixes that remove the need to reach for it. A callback that runs while the window exists but is not yet visible: ```rust WebviewWindowBuilder::new(app, "main", url) // Called on the window's own thread after CreateWindowExW has produced the // HWND (WM_CREATE would be ideal) and before the window is first shown. .on_window_created(|window: &Window| { /* raw HWND available here */ }) ``` ### Alternatives considered - **Build hidden, fix up, then show** (`.visible(false)` + `set_position` + icons + `show()`). This is the obvious answer and the one we would prefer, but `build()` also creates the WebView2 environment and controller, which takes the better part of a second. Deferring the first appearance until after `build()` returns means half a second of nothing on screen after the user launched the app. The window has to be visible *during* the build, which means its geometry, icon and activation have to be right *before* the build. - **`SetWindowSubclass` after `build()` returns.** Too late for everything above; the window has been shown. - **`RunEvent::WindowEvent` / `on_window_event` / the returned `WebviewWindow`.** All post-show. Correcting position or maximized state from there is visible as a jump or an animation, which is what we are trying to eliminate. ### Additional context Versions: `tauri 2.11.5`, `tauri-runtime-wry 2.11.4`, `tao 0.35.3`, `wry 0.55.1`, Windows 11.

### Describe the problem

An app that resolves keyboard shortcuts itself cannot let the OS run a menu item's accelerator. The OS decides on the item's enabled state alone, and never consults the app's own condition for the shortcut.

We build our menubar from JS through `@tauri-apps/api/menu`. `MenuItem`'s handler is `action?: (id: string) => void`, so there is no way to tell a click from an accelerator, and therefore no way to route an accelerator through our own resolver while still running the command on click.

A concrete misfire from our app. `Edit > Clear` is bound to `Delete` and is enabled whenever the grid is writable. Our keybinding additionally requires the grid to hold focus, because `Delete` belongs to the text caret when focus is in a text input. With the caret in our Find field, pressing `Delete` clears grid cells instead of deleting a character.

Full motivation is in tauri-apps/muda#393.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Once muda reports it, surface it in both layers:

- `crates/tauri/src/menu/` on the `MenuEvent` the app receives
- `packages/api/src/menu/menuItem.ts`, e.g. widening the callback to `(event: { id: string; triggeredByAccelerator: boolean }) => void` alongside the current signature

This is what Electron exposes as `KeyboardEvent.triggeredByAccelerator`, and what VS Code's menubar is built on.

### Alternatives considered

Gating the accelerator with `setAccelerator(null)` whenever the keybinding's condition is false. This works today with no upstream change, but on macOS the accelerator is also the display, so the shortcut disappears from the menu while the item stays enabled and clickable.

### Additional context

Opening this as a suggestion issue first, per CONTRIBUTING. Glad to do the work if the direction is agreeable.

- `crates/tauri/src/menu/` on the `MenuEvent` the app receives
- `packages/api/src/menu/menuItem.ts`, e.g. widening the callback to `(event: { id: string; triggeredByAccelerator: boolean }) => void` alongside the current signature

This is what Electron exposes as `KeyboardEvent.triggeredByAccelerator`, and what VS Code's menubar is built on.

### Alternatives considered

Gating the accelerator with `setAccelerator(null)` whenever the keybinding's condition is false. This works today with no upstream change, but on macOS the accelerator is also the display, so the shortcut disappears from the menu while the item stays enabled and clickable.

### Additional context

Opening this as a suggestion issue first, per CONTRIBUTING. Glad to do the work if the direction is agreeable.
