body_text:
## Summary

Tauri CLI 2.12.1 rejects a fresh official v1 starter whose Cargo manifest uses `tauri = { version = "1", features = ["shell-open"] }` when no Cargo lockfile supplies a resolved version. `"1"` is a valid Cargo version requirement. Migration attempts to parse that requirement as a complete semantic version and exits before migrating the app.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a disposable v1 project with `npm exec --yes --package=create-tauri-app@4.7.4 -- create-tauri-app migration-repro --tauri-version 1 --template vanilla-ts --manager npm --identifier com.example.migrationrepro --yes`.
2. Confirm that `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` contains the starter's `tauri` version requirement `"1"` and that the disposable project has no `Cargo.lock`. Do not build or run Cargo dependency resolution before this check.
3. From the generated project, run the v2 CLI's `migrate` command with `npm exec --yes --package=@tauri-apps/cli@2.12.1 -- tauri migrate`.
4. In a second fresh disposable copy, change only the `tauri` dependency requirement from `"1"` to `"1.8.3"` and run the same migration command. This control passed migration in the recorded run.

## Expected behavior

The migration command accepts the valid major-only Cargo requirement emitted by the official starter and selects the v1 migration, without requiring a preliminary build or a manual patch of the dependency requirement.

## Actual behavior

The `"1"` input fails semantic-version parsing before the v1 migration runs. The explicit `"1.8.3"` control passes migration. The retained execution record does not preserve the complete stderr or full `tauri info` transcript, so this report does not invent either output.

## Affected area

`crates/tauri-cli/src/migrate/mod.rs` obtains the dependency value through `crate_version` and calls `semver::Version::from_str`. When exactly one resolved package is absent from a lockfile, `crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/cargo_manifest.rs` returns the manifest's version requirement.

## Runtime or environment

Recorded execution used create-tauri-app 4.7.4, `@tauri-apps/cli` 2.12.1, macOS 27.0 build 26A428 on ARM64, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1, Node.js 22.23.2, and npm 12.0.2. The npm registry currently identifies CLI 2.12.1 as the stable `latest` version. This follow-up inspected current source and did not rerun native app builds.

## Evidence

- [Migration source at the inspected revision](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/30da1fd6e17de6107ecc850c95dfb16b5729f2dd/crates/tauri-cli/src/migrate/mod.rs#L48) parses the selected value as a `semver::Version`.
- [Version lookup at the same revision](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/30da1fd6e17de6107ecc850c95dfb16b5729f2dd/crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/cargo_manifest.rs#L151) falls back to the manifest requirement when no single locked version is available.
- [Official starter manifest](https://github.com/tauri-apps/create-tauri-app/blob/12db955f20162e7422cbeed76c2aa630760ccca3/templates/_base_/src-tauri/Cargo.toml.lte) emits the valid v1 requirement `"1"`.
- [Cargo version requirement documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#version-requirement-syntax) permits major-only requirements.

## Impact

A freshly generated v1 app cannot enter the documented migration workflow until its dependency is resolved into a lockfile or the requirement is manually changed.

## Additional context

The issue belongs to migration handling because the starter emits a valid Cargo requirement. A regression check is red when a v1 manifest with requirement `"1"` and no lockfile fails version detection, and green when it reaches the v1 migration. Retain the explicit-version control so parsing valid Cargo requirements does not break ordinary complete-version inputs. This differs from issue #13819, which concerns a v2 alpha project and config migration.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

On Linux, a `tauri-runtime-cef` app never gets a hardware WebGPU adapter. With the
Chromium switches that make WebGPU work in stock Chrome on the same machine,
`navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` returns only SwiftShader (`vendor: google`,
`architecture: swiftshader`, `isFallbackAdapter: true`).

Plain CEF from the **same CEF build** (`cefsimple` from the official
`cef_binary_152.0.6+g708dc14+chromium-152.0.7977.83_linux64_client`
distribution), on the same machine, with the same switches and the same X11
ozone platform, returns the Intel GPU (`vendor: intel`, `architecture: gen-9`,
`isFallbackAdapter: false`). So this looks specific to how `tauri-runtime-cef`
sets CEF up, not to CEF or Chromium.

Separately, `enable-unsafe-webgpu` passed through `Cef::command_line_arg` seems to
have no effect at all: with it, not even the SwiftShader fallback adapter is
offered. Passing the same switch on the process command line (with
`Cef::allow_chromium_command_line_args(true)`) does make the fallback appear.

### Reproduction

Versions: `tauri` 3.0.0-alpha.4, `tauri-runtime-cef` 3.0.0-alpha.5 (`cef =152.3.0`,
CEF 152.0.6, Chromium 152.0.7977.83), `tauri-build` 3.0.0-alpha.3, CLI 3.0.0-alpha.4.

`src/main.rs` (the rest is a default `tauri.conf.json` with one window, `frontendDist`
pointing at a page that runs the snippet below):

```rust
use tauri_runtime_cef::{Cef, RemoteDebugging, SandboxPolicy};

#[tauri_runtime_cef::cef_entry_point]
fn main() {
  let cef = Cef::default()
    // Ubuntu 24.04 restricts unprivileged user namespaces; disabled only so the
    // unbundled binary starts. The AppImage behaves the same with sandbox `auto`
    // once its AppArmor prompt is declined.
    .sandbox(SandboxPolicy::Disabled)
    .enable_features(["Vulkan"])                 // merged, per switches.rs
    .command_line_arg("enable-unsafe-webgpu", None::<String>)
    .remote_debugging(RemoteDebugging::Port { port: 20071, allowed_origins: vec![] });
  tauri::Builder::default()
    .runtime(cef)
    .run(tauri::generate_context!())
    .expect("run");
}
```

Page:

```js
const a = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter({ powerPreference: 'high-performance' });
console.log(a ? JSON.stringify({ vendor: a.info.vendor, arch: a.info.architecture, fallback: a.info.isFallbackAdapter }) : 'no adapter');
```

### Results (same machine, same session, X11 via XWayland unless noted)

| Host | WebGPU switches | Adapter |
|---|---|---|
| `tauri-runtime-cef` app | none | none ("No available adapters") |
| `tauri-runtime-cef` app | `enable_features(["Vulkan"])` + `command_line_arg("enable-unsafe-webgpu")` | **none** |
| `tauri-runtime-cef` app | `enable_features(["Vulkan"])` + `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` as argv (`allow_chromium_command_line_args(true)`) | **SwiftShader only** |
| `cefsimple` (CEF 152.0.6 client distribution) | none | none |
| `cefsimple` | `--enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan --ozone-platform=x11` | **Intel gen-9** (also with `--use-alloy-style`) |
| Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.83 | `--enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan` (X11 or Wayland) | **Intel gen-9** |

In every `tauri-runtime-cef` run, `SystemInfo.getInfo` reports `webgpu: enabled`,
`vulkan: enabled_on`, and WebGL2 is hardware
(`ANGLE (Intel, Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 630 (KBL GT2), OpenGL 4.6)`).

### One structural difference I noticed (not proven to be the cause)

`cefsimple` runs a normal `--type=gpu-process` child, plus `--type=renderer` and
`--type=utility` children. The `tauri-runtime-cef` app shows **no**
`--type=gpu-process` or `--type=renderer` processes at all, only zygote-forked
processes and one utility process. One of those zygote forks maps the system
`libvulkan_intel.so` (and SwiftShader), so the Intel ICD is loaded, but Dawn does
not offer it.

### Expected behavior

With the same switches, `tauri-runtime-cef` should enumerate the same adapters as
plain CEF from the same distribution. And `Cef::command_line_arg("enable-unsafe-webgpu")`
should have the same effect as the switch on the command line.

### Platform and versions

- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-31, glibc 2.39
- Intel Core i7-7700HQ, Intel HD Graphics 630 (i915, Mesa 25.2.8). An NVIDIA GTX
  1060 Mobile is present but has no driver loaded.
- GNOME 46 on Wayland. The runtime forces `--ozone-platform=x11`, so XWayland.
- Rust 1.97.1

### Additional context

On Windows (RTX 3080), the same app gets a hardware adapter with default
settings, and render, compute and present all verify. So this is Linux-only.

Related, and not a Tauri issue: on this GPU, stock Chrome's WebGPU canvas
presentation stalls under X11 while working under native Wayland, and CEF warns
`'--ozone-platform=wayland' is not compatible with Vulkan`. I'm noting it only
because the runtime is X11-only on Linux, so even with an adapter, presentation
may need more work there.

### Describe the bug

`tauri build --bundles appimage` for a `tauri-runtime-cef` app fails on Linux with:

```
failed to bundle project: quick-sharun command failed to run.
...
 Download failed! Trying again...   (x5)
 ERROR: Failed to download 5 times!
```

`crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/sharun_cef.rs` (still the case
at `v3` head, `a8703ee4`) downloads
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabianLars/Anylinux-AppImages/refs/heads/main/useful-tools/quick-sharun.sh`
at build time. That fork is 133 commits behind `pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages`,
and its script still points at upstream `main` for two C sources it compiles:

```
ANYLINUX_LIB_SOURCE  = .../pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/refs/heads/main/useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c
GTK_CLASS_FIX_SOURCE = .../pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/refs/heads/main/useful-tools/lib/gtk-class-fix.c
```

Upstream removed both on 2026-09-10 (pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages@e3de1528,
"helper libs are now hosted in Anylinux-sharun, add checksum checks to all file
downloads"), so both URLs return 404. Every CEF AppImage build fails this way.
The fork has issues disabled, so I'm reporting it here.

### Reproduction

Any `tauri-runtime-cef` app on Linux: `tauri build --bundles appimage`.

```
$ curl -sL -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/refs/heads/main/useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c
404
```

### Workaround

The script honours both variables, so pinning them to the upstream commit the
fork last merged (`d1bb2688`) gets a working bundle:

```sh
U=d1bb26882eded9576bb0760aeb848179bbf64e9b
export ANYLINUX_LIB_SOURCE=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/$U/useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c
export GTK_CLASS_FIX_SOURCE=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/$U/useful-tools/lib/gtk-class-fix.c
tauri build --bundles appimage
```

### Expected behavior

The bundle builds without depending on files that can disappear from another
repository's `main`. Pinning the script (and the sources it fetches) to a
commit, or vendoring it, would also make bundles reproducible. Currently a
change in either repository changes what gets shipped.

### Platform and versions

Ubuntu 24.04.4, `tauri-cli` 3.0.0-alpha.4, `tauri-bundler` 3.0.0-alpha.3,
`tauri-runtime-cef` 3.0.0-alpha.5. With the workaround, the resulting AppImage
(about 175 MiB) launches and loads its page.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

On Linux, a `tauri-runtime-cef` app maps its window immediately at creation even when the builder sets `visible(false)`. Because the CEF browser surface is composited onto that window, the first thing users see is a plain white canvas (light color scheme) or a near-black one (dark scheme) — regardless of the background color the app configures. The themed content only appears once the page finishes loading, so the visible sequence is: white box → (themed content), lasting from window creation until first content paint. On slower machines this is several seconds; on fast ones a few hundred milliseconds.

We maintain a Tauri app (Readest) that shows its main window only after the frontend has painted the themed background, so we instrumented this heavily (frame-by-frame window sampling at ~70 ms intervals via screen capture, plus color-layer probes). What we can confirm from the outside:

- `visible(false)` at creation: the window is still mapped (verified via `GetWindowRect`-style sampling from the compositor and window enumeration — the mapped window appears at the WM-assigned position immediately after `create_window` returns, before any app code can move it).
- A dispatcher-routed `set_position(-32000, -32000)` issued right after `build()` lands **after** the first presented frame (~250–500 ms later), so post-creation moves cannot prevent the initial flash.
- `BrowserSettings.background_color` did not appear in the visible frames in our setup (we probed with a magenta background color and saw neither it nor our themed color during the startup window — though the probe build simultaneously parked the window off-screen, so we can't fully separate the layers).
- Calling `Window::hide()` right after `build()` on the upstream winit-gtk4 runtime (which implements `Hide` via `set_visible(false)`) does remove the white box — but the unmap makes CEF flag `WasHidden`, which throttles rendering and stalls the page load we are waiting for, so the window stays invisible for the entire load (worse than the flash).

So the visible sequence on the current runtime is: window maps (white canvas) → [our app paints its themed frame] → themed content. The window cannot be kept unmapped during the load, and nothing we set makes the pre-paint canvas match our theme.

### Reproduction

Any `tauri-runtime-cef` app whose builder sets `visible(false)` and whose frontend paints a dark background on a light-system (or vice versa) reproduces the flash. The essential shape:

```rust
tauri::Builder::default()
  .runtime(tauri_runtime_cef::Cef::default())
  .setup(|app| {
    tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder::new(app, "main", tauri::WebviewUrl::App("index.html".into()))
      .visible(false)          // observed: window still maps
      .background_color(Some(Color(0x2f, 0x2f, 0x2f, 0xff)))  // observed: canvas still white
      .build()?;
    Ok(())
  })
  .run(tauri::generate_context!())
  .expect("run");
```

Plus an HTML frontend that sets a themed background after load. Launching on a light-system desktop with a dark-themed frontend shows the white canvas before the themed frame.

body_text:
## Describe the bug

With `app.security.pattern.use = "isolation"`, **every** `invoke()` hangs forever on Windows. No
error is thrown, no promise rejects, and nothing is logged on either the JS or the Rust side.

The cause is in `crates/tauri/scripts/isolation.js`. The isolation iframe is created with
`allow-scripts` and nothing else:

```js
let iframe = document.createElement('iframe')
iframe.id = '__tauri_isolation__'
iframe.sandbox.add('allow-scripts')     // <- no allow-same-origin
iframe.src = __TEMPLATE_isolation_src__
```

A sandboxed iframe without `allow-same-origin` is assigned an **opaque origin**. On Windows (and
Android) the isolation frame is navigated to `http://<schema>.localhost`
(`crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs`, `format_real_schema`), and the resulting frame **is not a secure
context**, so `window.crypto.subtle` is `undefined`.

That breaks the isolation payload script, which needs SubtleCrypto to import the AES-GCM key:

```js
// crates/tauri-utils/src/pattern/isolation.js
const aesGcmKey = await window.crypto.subtle.importKey(
  'raw', aesGcmKeyRaw, 'AES-GCM', false, ['encrypt']
)
```

### Why it fails *silently* — this is the part that makes it expensive to debug

Three things compound:

1. `crates/tauri-utils/src/pattern/isolation.js` is an **async IIFE with no `try`/`catch`**. The
   `importKey` above rejects, the IIFE's promise rejects as an unhandled rejection **inside a
   sandboxed iframe**, and the `setTimeout(waitUntilReady, readyIntervalMs)` at the bottom of the
   file is never reached — so `__TAURI_ISOLATION_READY__` is never posted to the parent.
2. In `crates/tauri/scripts/ipc.js`, the `case 'isolation'` branch does
   `if (isolation.ready) sendIsolationMessage(message) else isolation.queue.push(message)`, and
   `isolation.ready` is only ever set by the `__TAURI_ISOLATION_READY__` listener. So
   **`isolation.queue` grows without bound and is never flushed.**
3. Therefore every `invoke()` promise is **pending forever**. There is nothing to `catch`, no Rust
   log line (nothing reaches Rust), and no error boundary fires. Only a timeout can observe it.

Downstream this presents as unrelated-looking failures: OAuth never starts (`shell:open` is IPC),
the SQL plugin never creates its database, keychain commands never return — all one root cause.

## Reproduction

### Minimal, no Tauri required

This isolates the web-platform mechanism. Serve two files over plain `http` and open `parent.html`:

```html
<!-- parent.html -->
<script>
  const i = document.createElement('iframe')
  i.sandbox.add('allow-scripts')           // flip: also add 'allow-same-origin'
  i.src = 'http://localhost:8791/child.html'
  document.body.appendChild(i)
</script>
```

```html
<!-- child.html -->
<script>
  parent.postMessage({
    origin: location.origin,               // "null" == opaque
    isSecureContext: window.isSecureContext,
    subtle: typeof (window.crypto && window.crypto.subtle)
  }, '*')
</script>
```

With `allow-scripts` only the child reports an opaque origin; adding `allow-same-origin` gives it
its real origin, `isSecureContext: true` and a working `crypto.subtle`.

### In Tauri

1. `tauri.conf.json` → `"app": { "security": { "pattern": { "use": "isolation" } } }`.
2. Build and run a **release** build on Windows.
3. Launch with `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222`, attach over
   CDP, and read `isSecureContext` + `typeof crypto.subtle` per frame.
4. Call any `invoke()` from the frontend — the promise never settles.

### Measured

| Frame | Origin | `isSecureContext` | `crypto.subtle` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `http://tauri.localhost` | `true` | `object` |
| isolation | `http://isolation-<uuid>.localhost` | **`false`** | **`undefined`** |

…with a live `pageerror` from the isolation frame:
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'importKey')`.

## Expected behavior

The isolation frame should be a secure context so its AES-GCM key bootstrap succeeds and IPC works;
failing that, the key bootstrap should fail **loudly** rather than leaving every `invoke()` pending.

## Platform

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 19045, WebView2
- `tauri`: 2.11.6 (line is identical in 2.11.5 and unchanged on `dev`)
- Pattern: `isolation`
- macOS/Linux are **not** affected: `format_real_schema` gives those platforms a Tauri-registered
  custom scheme (`<schema>://localhost`) rather than `http://<schema>.localhost`.

## Related

- #10956 — "Refused to execute inline script in isolation mode", Windows/WebView2, open since
  2024-09-11, `status: needs triage`. A second Windows-specific isolation defect.
- `tauri-apps/wry` #1710 / #1709 — the same bug class already accepted for Android: Android WebView
  excludes `http://tauri.localhost` from secure contexts, blocking secure-context APIs.

## Suggested fix

Add `allow-same-origin` to the isolation iframe's sandbox (PR below). The frame keeps a **different
origin** from the main frame (`<schema>.localhost` vs `tauri.localhost`), so the two remain
cross-origin and `postMessage` stays the only channel.

### Two secondary issues worth fixing alongside

1. **The payload script has no error handling.** Wrapping the IIFE in `try`/`catch` and posting a
   failure message to the parent would have turned this from a silent hang into a one-line
   diagnosis. Worth doing *independently of* the sandbox fix.
2. **`frame-src` is never widened for the isolation origin.** For the main document,
   `crates/tauri/src/manager/mod.rs` pushes the isolation origin into **`default-src` only**. An
   app whose configured CSP sets an explicit `frame-src` (e.g. `frame-src 'none'`, which is
   otherwise good hygiene) will have the isolation iframe blocked outright, because an explicit
   `frame-src` suppresses the `default-src` fallback. Either inject into `frame-src` as well, or
   document that `frame-src` must not be set when using the isolation pattern.

{"repository": "tauri-apps/tauri", "task_candidate_id": 24759, "repository_id": 292, "issue_number": 16219, "github_issue_id": 5735720545, "html_url": "https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/16219", "created_at": "2026-10-06T21:34:32+00:00", "author_association": "NONE", "title": "[bug] Isolation pattern: the isolation iframe gets an opaque origin, so crypto.subtle is undefined and ALL IPC silently hangs (Windows/WebView2)", "body_text": "## Describe the bug

With `app.security.pattern.use = "isolation"`, **every** `invoke()` hangs forever on Windows. No
error is thrown, no promise rejects, and nothing is logged on either the JS or the Rust side.

The cause is in `crates/tauri/scripts/isolation.js`. The isolation iframe is created with
`allow-scripts` and nothing else:

```js
let iframe = document.createElement('iframe')
iframe.id = '__tauri_isolation__'
iframe.sandbox.add('allow-scripts')     // <- no allow-same-origin
iframe.src = __TEMPLATE_isolation_src__
```

A sandboxed iframe without `allow-same-origin` is assigned an **opaque origin**. On Windows (and
Android) the isolation frame is navigated to `http://<schema>.localhost`
(`crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs`, `format_real_schema`), and the resulting frame **is not a secure
context**, so `window.crypto.subtle` is `undefined`.

That breaks the isolation payload script, which needs SubtleCrypto to import the AES-GCM key:

```js
// crates/tauri-utils/src/pattern/isolation.js
const aesGcmKey = await window.crypto.subtle.importKey(
  'raw', aesGcmKeyRaw, 'AES-GCM', false, ['encrypt']
)
```

### Why it fails *silently* — this is the part that makes it expensive to debug

Three things compound:

1. `crates/tauri-utils/src/pattern/isolation.js` is an **async IIFE with no `try`/`catch`**. The
   `importKey` above rejects, the IIFE's promise rejects as an unhandled rejection **inside a
   sandboxed iframe**, and the `setTimeout(waitUntilReady, readyIntervalMs)` at the bottom of the
   file is never reached — so `__TAURI_ISOLATION_READY__` is never posted to the parent.
2. In `crates/tauri/scripts/ipc.js`, the `case 'isolation'` branch does
   `if (isolation.ready) sendIsolationMessage(message) else isolation.queue.push(message)`, and
   `isolation.ready` is only ever set by the `__TAURI_ISOLATION_READY__` listener. So
   **`isolation.queue` grows without bound and is never flushed.**
3. Therefore every `invoke()` promise is **pending forever**. There is nothing to `catch`, no Rust
   log line (nothing reaches Rust), and no error boundary fires. Only a timeout can observe it.

Downstream this presents as unrelated-looking failures: OAuth never starts (`shell:open` is IPC),
the SQL plugin never creates its database, keychain commands never return — all one root cause.

## Reproduction

### Minimal, no Tauri required

This isolates the web-platform mechanism. Serve two files over plain `http` and open `parent.html`:

```html
<!-- parent.html -->
<script>
  const i = document.createElement('iframe')
  i.sandbox.add('allow-scripts')           // flip: also add 'allow-same-origin'
  i.src = 'http://localhost:8791/child.html'
  document.body.appendChild(i)
</script>
```

```html
<!-- child.html -->
<script>
  parent.postMessage({
    origin: location.origin,               // "null" == opaque
    isSecureContext: window.isSecureContext,
    subtle: typeof (window.crypto && window.crypto.subtle)
  }, '*')
</script>
```

With `allow-scripts` only the child reports an opaque origin; adding `allow-same-origin` gives it
its real origin, `isSecureContext: true` and a working `crypto.subtle`.

### In Tauri

1. `tauri.conf.json` → `"app": { "security": { "pattern": { "use": "isolation" } } }`.
2. Build and run a **release** build on Windows.
3. Launch with `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222`, attach over
   CDP, and read `isSecureContext` + `typeof crypto.subtle` per frame.
4. Call any `invoke()` from the frontend — the promise never settles.

### Measured

| Frame | Origin | `isSecureContext` | `crypto.subtle` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `http://tauri.localhost` | `true` | `object` |
| isolation | `http://isolation-<uuid>.localhost` | **`false`** | **`undefined`** |

…with a live `pageerror` from the isolation frame:
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'importKey')`.

## Expected behavior

The isolation frame should be a secure context so its AES-GCM key bootstrap succeeds and IPC works;
failing that, the key bootstrap should fail **loudly** rather than leaving every `invoke()` pending.

## Platform

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 19045, WebView2
- `tauri`: 2.11.6 (line is identical in 2.11.5 and unchanged on `dev`)
- Pattern: `isolation`
- macOS/Linux are **not** affected: `format_real_schema` gives those platforms a Tauri-registered
  custom scheme (`<schema>://localhost`) rather than `http://<schema>.localhost`.

## Related

- #10956 — "Refused to execute inline script in isolation mode", Windows/WebView2, open since
  2024-09-11, `status: needs triage`. A second Windows-specific isolation defect.
- `tauri-apps/wry` #1710 / #1709 — the same bug class already accepted for Android: Android WebView
  excludes `http://tauri.localhost` from secure contexts, blocking secure-context APIs.

## Suggested fix

Add `allow-same-origin` to the isolation iframe's sandbox (PR below). The frame keeps a **different
origin** from the main frame (`<schema>.localhost` vs `tauri.localhost`), so the two remain
cross-origin and `postMessage` stays the only channel.

### Two secondary issues worth fixing alongside

1. **The payload script has no error handling.** Wrapping the IIFE in `try`/`catch` and posting a
   failure message to the parent would have turned this from a silent hang into a one-line
   diagnosis. Worth doing *independently of* the sandbox fix.
2. **`frame-src` is never widened for the isolation origin.** For the main document,
   `crates/tauri/src/manager/mod.rs` pushes the isolation origin into **`default-src` only**. An
   app whose configured CSP sets an explicit `frame-src` (e.g. `frame-src 'none'`, which is
   otherwise good hygiene) will have the isolation iframe blocked outright, because an explicit
   `frame-src` suppresses the `default-src` fallback. Either inject into `frame-src` as well, or
   document that `frame-src` must not be set when using the isolation pattern.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

On Linux, a `tauri-runtime-cef` app never receives renderer keyboard events for combos that match Chromium's browser-accelerator table. The keydown is consumed in the browser process before it reaches the page, and on a quick tap **the keyup is swallowed too** — the entire gesture is invisible to JavaScript.

Observed with `Ctrl+Shift+T` (a registered Chromium accelerator — "reopen closed tab"):

- Quick tap: modifier keydowns (`Control`, `Shift`) arrive, but there is **no keydown and no keyup** for the `T` key at any point. No JS event for the letter ever fires.
- Hold: the first `T` event the page receives is `repeat=true` (OS auto-repeat); the keyup arrives only when the key is finally released.
- Unrelated combos (e.g. `Ctrl+P` in our setup) are delivered normally — keydown and keyup both arrive immediately.

We verified this with renderer-side `window` `keydown`/`keyup` listeners instrumented to log `key`, `code`, modifiers and `repeat` (see Stack trace). The app has input focus (a click inside the window before pressing, and the modifier keydowns reaching the page, both confirm this).

Consequence: any in-renderer keybinding resolver — the standard VS Code-style architecture, and the only one Tauri supports since no native key interception is exposed — never sees the first press. The binding fires only when OS key auto-repeat eventually leaks a `repeat=true` event, i.e. the user must hold the key. On a quick tap there is no JS-visible event at all to recover from, so the shortcut is silently dead and no frontend workaround is possible.

### Reproduction

Any Tauri app using the CEF runtime with a renderer-side key listener:

```rust
tauri::Builder::default()
  .runtime(tauri_runtime_cef::Cef::default())
  .run(tauri::generate_context!())
  .expect("error while running tauri application");
```

```js
// in the frontend
window.addEventListener('keydown', e =>
  console.log('[diag] keydown', e.key, e.code, 'ctrl', e.ctrlKey, 'shift', e.shiftKey, 'repeat', e.repeat));
window.addEventListener('keyup', e =>
  console.log('[diag] keyup', e.key, e.code, 'ctrl', e.ctrlKey, 'shift', e.shiftKey));
```

1. Click inside the window (give it input focus).
2. Press `Ctrl+Shift+T` quickly (tap, do not hold).

Expected: a `keydown` event with `key === "T"`. Actual: nothing for the `T` key — only the `Control` and `Shift` keydowns appear. Holding the combo produces only `repeat=true` keydowns followed by the keyup on release.

### Expected behavior

The keydown should reach the renderer so the application can handle it — this is what the wry/WebKitGTK runtime does for the same combo, so this is a cross-runtime behavioral divergence with no app-level workaround.

Alternatively, if accelerator consumption is considered correct CEF behavior, the runtime should expose a way to opt out, as comparable webviews do:

- **WebView2**: `AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled(false)` — "disables all accelerator keys that access browser features… so web content receives the keydown"
- **Electron**: `webContents.on('before-input-event', (event, input) => event.preventDefault())` — fires before the renderer, in the main process
- **CEF itself** provides the equivalent hook internally: `CefKeyboardHandler::OnPreKeyEvent`. `tauri-runtime-cef` already implements this handler (to block F12 / Ctrl+Shift+I when devtools are disabled), but the handler is hardcoded and not exposed to application code.

### Full `tauri info` output

```
[✔] Environment
    - OS: Linux Unknown x86_64 (X64) (Hyprland on wayland)
    ✔ webkit2gtk-4.1: 2.52.6
    ✔ rsvg2: 2.62.4
    ✔ rustc: 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
    ✔ cargo: 1.99.0 (5f94df478 2026-08-27)
    ✔ rustup: 1.29.1 (d95a37b6a 2026-08-13)
    ✔ Rust toolchain: 1.99.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (overridden by environment variable RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN)
    - node: 26.11.1
    - pnpm: 11.26.0
    - npm: 11.20.0
    - bun: 1.4.2
    - deno: deno 2.9.7

[-] Packages
    - tauri 🦀: 3.0.0-alpha
    - tauri-build 🦀: 3.0.0-alpha.3
    - wry 🦀: No version detected
    - tao 🦀: No version detected
    - @tauri-apps/api ⱼₛ: not installed!
    - @tauri-apps/cli ⱼₛ: 2.10.0 (outdated, latest: 2.12.1)

[-] App
    - build-type: bundle
    - CSP: unset
    - frontendDist: ../dist
    - devUrl: http://localhost:1420/
    - framework: React
    - bundler: Vite
```

Pinned runtime crates: `tauri-runtime-cef = "=3.0.0-alpha.5"` (features: `devtools`), `cef = 152.3.0+152.0.6`.

### Stack trace

Renderer instrumentation (`window` keydown/keyup listeners), quick tap of `Ctrl+Shift+T` — note there is no event for the letter in either direction:

```
[kb-diag] keydown key="Control" code="ControlLeft" ctrl=true  shift=false repeat=false
[kb-diag] keydown key="Shift"   code="ShiftLeft"   ctrl=true  shift=true  repeat=false
[kb-diag] keydown key="Control" code="ControlLeft" ctrl=true  shift=false repeat=false
[kb-diag] keydown key="Shift"   code="ShiftLeft"   ctrl=true  shift=true  repeat=false
                                                    ↑ modifiers arrive; no keydown/keyup for "T" at all
```

Holding the same combo — first delivered event for the letter is already an auto-repeat:

```
[kb-diag] keydown key="T" code="KeyT" ctrl=true shift=true repeat=true
[kb-diag] keydown key="T" code="KeyT" ctrl=true shift=true repeat=true   (…repeats while held…)
[kb-diag] keyup   key="T" code="KeyT" ctrl=true shift=true repeat=false  (arrives on release only)
```

For contrast, a quick tap of `Ctrl+P` in the same session is delivered normally:

```
[kb-diag] keydown key="p" code="KeyP" ctrl=true shift=false repeat=false
[kb-diag] keyup   key="p" code="KeyP" ctrl=true shift=false repeat=false
```

### Additional context

- This is not a focus or compositor artifact: the modifier keydowns reach the page, and the same-session `Ctrl+P` tap delivers keydown+keyup fine. Only the letter key of accelerator combos is missing, and it is missing on both press and release for a quick tap.
- `tauri-plugin-prevent-default` covers the wry runtime (its `browser_accelerator_keys` option maps to the WebView2 API), but it is typed `TauriPlugin<tauri::Wry>` and does not address CEF's accelerator handling.
- Related issues: #7418 (feature request for disabling browser shortcuts), #12677 (expose native keyboard events — wry-only, blocked on a macOS content-view problem that does not apply to CEF).
- Possible solution directions (open to maintainer preference): since `tauri-runtime-cef` already installs an `OnPreKeyEvent` handler, exposing an app-level registration path (builder option or handler trait) that receives raw key + modifiers before accelerator processing — or an option to disable browser-accelerator consumption, mirroring WebView2's `AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled(false)` — would let applications forward these keys to their renderer-side resolver. We'd be happy to implement this as a PR if the direction gets a thumbs-up.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

When it rewrites the manifest, tauri-cli collects the `tauri` dependency from `[dependencies]` and from every `[target.'cfg(..)'.dependencies]` table, then merges all of their features into `Manifest::tauri_features` without evaluating the cfg. On Linux, bundling uses that set to decide whether the app has a tray, so a `tray-icon` feature enabled only for Windows is treated as enabled on Linux.

This has two outcomes on Linux:

- Without an appindicator library installed, bundling panics after the Rust build succeeds.
- With one installed, bundling succeeds, but the deb and rpm depend on appindicator and the AppImage ships it, although the binary does not use it.

This is a regression from #16109, first released in tauri-cli 2.12.0. Before it, `find_dependency` returned only the first matching section, so a top-level `tauri` entry hid the target entries. The merge itself has always ignored cfgs.

### Reproduction

1. Create a project with `npm create tauri-app@latest` (vanilla template).
2. Append this to `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`:

   ```toml
   [target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
   tauri = { version = "2", features = ["tray-icon"] }
   ```

3. On Linux without `libayatana-appindicator3-dev` or `libappindicator3-dev`, run `npm run tauri build -- --bundles deb`.

Results with the same project:

- tauri-cli 2.11.5 bundles the deb with no appindicator dependency.
- tauri-cli 2.12.0, 2.12.1 and 2.12.2 panic (see the stack trace below).
- With 2.12.1 and a pkg-config entry for `ayatana-appindicator3-0.1`, the deb gains `Depends: libayatana-appindicator3-1`.

### Expected behavior

Bundling only considers `tauri` features enabled for the build target. A Linux bundle neither requires nor depends on appindicator here.

### Full `tauri info` output

```text
[✔] Environment
    - OS: Ubuntu 24.4.0 x86_64 (X64) (Unknown DE on Unknown Session)
    ✔ webkit2gtk-4.1: 2.52.6
    ✔ rsvg2: 2.58.0
    ✔ rustc: 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
    ✔ cargo: 1.99.0 (5f94df478 2026-08-27)
    ✔ rustup: 1.29.1 (d95a37b6a 2026-08-13)
    ✔ Rust toolchain: stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (default)
    - node: 24.21.0
    - pnpm: 12.11.2
    - npm: 12.2.0

[-] Packages
    - tauri 🦀: 2.12.3
    - tauri-build 🦀: 2.7.2
    - wry 🦀: 0.57.0
    - tao 🦀: 0.37.1
    - @tauri-apps/api  ⱼₛ: not installed!
    - @tauri-apps/cli  ⱼₛ: 2.12.1 (outdated, latest: 2.12.2)

[-] Plugins
    - tauri-plugin-opener 🦀: 2.7.1
    - @tauri-apps/plugin-opener  ⱼₛ: not installed!

[-] App
    - build-type: bundle
    - CSP: unset
    - frontendDist: ../src
```

The same failure happens in CI on the GitHub `ubuntu-22.04` and `ubuntu-22.04-arm` runners.

### Stack trace

```text
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at crates/tauri-cli/src/interface/rust.rs:1702:17:
Can't detect any appindicator library
```

### Additional context

The merge happens in [`inject_features`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-cli-v2.12.2/crates/tauri-cli/src/interface/rust/manifest.rs#L238-L280), over the sections returned by [`find_dependency`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-cli-v2.12.2/crates/tauri-cli/src/interface/rust/manifest.rs#L115-L148). The [appindicator check](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-cli-v2.12.2/crates/tauri-cli/src/interface/rust.rs#L1353-L1379) is the only consumer of the merged set.

A possible fix leaves the write path of #16109 untouched and computes the enabled features where bundling needs them: read the rewritten manifest and only take the target sections that match the build target. Cargo's own `cargo-platform` crate can evaluate a section key against the output of `rustc --print cfg --target <triple>`, and it is already in the lockfile. Reading the resolved features from `cargo metadata --filter-platform <triple>` would be more precise, but it needs a full resolve.

The tray check also runs on the host's `cfg(target_os = "linux")` rather than the build target, as in #9598. That seems out of scope here.

As a stopgap, the CLI skips workspace-inherited entries, so declaring the target entry as `tauri = { workspace = true, features = ["tray-icon"] }` avoids the problem.

I'm happy to send a PR for the first approach if that direction works for you.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

On Linux (GTK/WebKitGTK), a window created with `decorations: false` cannot be resized by dragging its edges or corners at all. There is no resize band anywhere — not inside the window, not on its last pixel, not outside it.

This is not the "band is too narrow" complaint of tauri-apps/tao#1170 (which is about Windows): here the band does not exist.

tauri-apps/tauri#8519 reported undecorated windows being unresizable and was closed as completed in January 2024. The fix is present in the versions below, but the Linux case still behaves as described.

**The window manager is not the problem.** In the same session, on the same window, `getCurrentWindow().startResizeDragging(direction)` — which reaches `gtk_window_begin_resize_drag` — resizes the window correctly and follows the pointer. So the compositor honours the resize grab; what never happens is the hit-test that would start one. The press appears to be consumed before tao can act on it.

### Reproduction

1. Build a Tauri v2 app for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` with `"decorations": false` and `"resizable": true`.
2. Run it on a GTK desktop (details below) under X11.
3. Try to resize by dragging any edge or corner.

Measured rather than eyeballed — a synthetic pointer driver (XTest) walked the right-hand edge one pixel at a time and the window geometry was read with `xwininfo` before and after each drag:

```
offset -3 (inside the window)  unchanged
offset -2                      unchanged
offset -1                      unchanged
offset  0 (last window pixel)  unchanged
offset +1 (outside)            unchanged
offset +2                      unchanged
offset +4                      unchanged
offset +6                      unchanged
```

All eight directions were also tried, with the window placed clear of every screen edge so nothing could be clamped: 8 of 8 unchanged. The same harness, on the same machine, does produce geometry changes on an ordinary decorated window and on the same app once it calls `startResizeDragging` itself — so the harness is not the reason nothing moved.

### Expected behavior

An undecorated, resizable window resizes from its edges and corners like any other window, as it does on the other platforms and as tauri-apps/tauri#8519 intended.

### Full `tauri info` / environment

- tauri `2.11.5`, tao `0.35.3`
- Astra Linux SE 1.8.6 (Debian 12 based), fly-wm, X11
- WebKitGTK 2.50.6
- `decorations: false`, `resizable: true`, custom title bar in the web layer

### Note

Happy to test a patch on this environment — it is a VM that can be rebuilt and driven headlessly, so a candidate fix can be verified end to end quickly.

The [repository](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) was archived by
its owner on 2024-03-25 and is read-only. The last release is 0.2.11
(March 2024).

`unsafe-libyaml` is a machine translation of libyaml's C code into unsafe
Rust (c2rust). Bugs found in it will not be fixed upstream. It is used by
`serde_yaml` (itself deprecated) and by forks such as `serde_yaml_ng`.

## Alternatives

Consider a YAML parser written in safe Rust, for example:

- [saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/saphyr) ([serde-saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/serde-saphyr) for serde users)

### Describe the bug

With `decorations: false` on Linux, the webview's `touch-event` handler in tauri-runtime-wry (`undecorated_resizing.rs`, `attach_resize_handler`) calls `begin_resize_drag_for_device` for every touch event within `BORDERLESS_RESIZE_INSET` of the border, not only on touch down. One touch sends one `xdg_toplevel.resize` per event, all with the same serial:

```
wl_touch.down(313, ...)
 -> xdg_toplevel.resize(wl_seat, 313, 8)
 -> xdg_toplevel.resize(wl_seat, 313, 8)
 -> xdg_toplevel.resize(wl_seat, 313, 8)
```

The first resize makes the compositor cancel the touch, so the rest ask for a touch that's already gone. On GNOME 50 that crashes gnome-shell and the whole session goes down (mutter bug https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/mutter/-/work_items/4871, fix in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/mutter/-/merge_requests/5375). The app shouldn't send them either way.

Still there in tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.1 and on `dev`. tao has the same handler on the GtkWindow, reported in tauri-apps/tao.

### Reproduction

1. `npm create tauri-app@latest`, set `"decorations": false` on the window in `tauri.conf.json`.
2. Run it on GNOME (Wayland) with a touchscreen: `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client npm run tauri dev`.
3. Put a finger on the window's edge and move it a bit.
4. The log shows several `xdg_toplevel.resize` with the same touch serial. On mutter 50.x without the fix above, gnome-shell segfaults.

### Expected behavior

One resize per touch, started on `TouchBegin` only, and the rest of that touch not turned into more requests.

### Describe the bug

On Linux, after a clean build of the minimal Tauri app below, the next `cargo build` with no changes recompiles the app crate; the third build is fresh. `cargo build -v` says a file in the crate's `OUT_DIR` changed after the last build, either the embedded copy of a frontend asset or the decoded app icon.

`generate_context!` creates those cached files during macro expansion and reuses unchanged contents ([`Cached`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-codegen-v2.7.3/crates/tauri-codegen/src/lib.rs#L118-L152), [`embedded_assets.rs`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-codegen-v2.7.3/crates/tauri-codegen/src/embedded_assets.rs#L354-L355)), and embeds them with `include_bytes!`, so they appear in the crate's dep-info. On a clean build they're created partway through compiling the crate, after the start time Cargo records for that compilation, so the next build sees them as changed. With unchanged inputs and intact cache files, neither path rewrites its output, so later builds are fresh.

In this minimal repro, that's one extra compilation of the app crate. In the larger app where I noticed it, the first unchanged build took 13.9 s wall time.

### Reproduction

A minimal app with Tauri 2.12.4 and tauri-build 2.7.3 (which resolved tauri-codegen 2.7.3), built with Rust 1.99.1:

`Cargo.toml`
```toml
[package]
name = "codegen-rebuild"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "=2.7.3", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "=2.12.4", features = [] }
```

`build.rs`
```rust
fn main() {
    tauri_build::build()
}
```

`src/main.rs`
```rust
fn main() {
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .run(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("error while running tauri application");
}
```

`tauri.conf.json`
```json
{
  "productName": "codegen-rebuild",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "identifier": "com.example.codegen-rebuild",
  "build": { "frontendDist": "dist" },
  "app": { "windows": [] },
  "bundle": { "icon": ["icons/icon.png"] }
}
```

`capabilities/default.json`
```json
{
  "identifier": "default",
  "windows": ["main"],
  "permissions": []
}
```

`dist/index.html`
```html
<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>repro</title></head><body>hello</body></html>
```

`icons/icon.png` is any RGBA PNG (I used a 32×32 one).

```sh
cargo clean -p codegen-rebuild
cargo build      # clean build of the app crate
cargo build -v   # no changes: recompiles codegen-rebuild
cargo build -v   # no changes: Fresh
```

Output of the last two builds on Rust 1.99.1, trimmed to the app crate:

```
Dirty codegen-rebuild v0.1.0 (~/…/codegen-rebuild): the file `target/debug/build/codegen-rebuild-378ecf376075a4bc/out/tauri-codegen-assets/67a2c487d3a03118fc02417087a719198132f1e3a1c50d0ccb170aee8327ff38.html` has changed (1792229579.036297851s, 1s after last build at 1792229578.964541273s)
Compiling codegen-rebuild v0.1.0 (~/…/codegen-rebuild)

Fresh codegen-rebuild v0.1.0 (~/…/codegen-rebuild)
```

The output directory also has the decoded icon (`out/7a0217859337fff31cfe7943567ebf63d016faf124c59a23b1da4c5e24800f16`, 4096 bytes = 32×32×4 for RGBA8). In nine runs of these steps on Rust 1.96.0 and 1.99.1, build 2 always recompiled and build 3 was always fresh; Cargo named the HTML asset eight times and the icon once.

### Expected behavior

The first unchanged `cargo build` immediately after the clean build (build 2 above) is a no-op.

body_text:
### Describe the problem
I recently experienced a catastrophic loss of my project data (a complex 3D location scene) solely due to Tauri's implicit data storage behavior during development. 

While working on a project, any reasonable developer expects all local database changes, states, and app data generated during `tauri dev` to remain strictly within the project directory. Instead, Tauri silently routes `appDataDir`, SQLite plugins, and Webview caches to OS system directories (`~/.local/share` on Linux, `AppData` on Windows). 

My system SSD crashed completely. Because my project folder was backed up on a separate drive, I thought my work was safe. It wasn't. The actual data database was silently buried deep inside `~/.local/share` without any explicit warning in the core documentation for beginners. Months of 3D environment work are now completely gone.

### Why this is a terrible developer experience (UX)
1. **Zero Portability by Default:** You cannot just copy a Tauri project folder to another machine or a backup drive and expect it to have the actual state/data of your app.
2. **Silent Storage Pollution:** Tauri treats the developer's machine as a production environment, cluttering system disks with hidden caches and local databases that are left behind forever when the project folder is deleted.
3. **Severe Data Risks:** When a system drive dies, developers lose their local databases because Tauri hid them away from the actual workspace.

### Suggested Solution / Feedback
Tauri needs to implement a dedicated **"Portable/Development Mode"** out of the box. 

When running `tauri dev`, ALL data, databases, logs, and Webview profiles must be strictly contained within the active project directory (e.g., inside `.tauri/dev_data/` or `src-tauri/target/`). If your architectural excuse is "OS security standards," remember that this is a *local development environment*, not a locked-down production bundle in `C:\Program Files`. 

Please stop copying Electron's worst habits blindly. Protect the developer's data first. I am completely abandoning Tauri for my future projects because of this flawed architecture, but I hope you fix this so other developers don't lose months of hard work.

body_text: ### Describe the bug We received a production report of a long-lived, borderless transparent desktop-pet window developing an opaque black rectangle in the areas that should show the desktop. The character itself remains visible in different animation poses, and window interactions still work. The window initially renders correctly. The report describes the problem as occurring after the app has been running for a while, but elapsed time has not been established as a necessary condition. We have **not reproduced the production failure through normal local system operations yet**, and we do not have a confirmed upstream root cause. This may be related to #15947, which concerns Windows 10 and frequent cursor-event toggles/minimize operations. Our report is on Windows 11, with display/device-change events present in the captured session. We cannot establish the exact user operation or the time when transparency first failed. Please also note the fork/version limitations in the environment section below. We are reporting an observed production failure and diagnostic results, not asserting that the latest unmodified upstream release has a confirmed defect. **Additional native customization:** this application uses `SetWindowRgn` plus custom non-client message handling; details and code are included below. Their contribution to the failure is not yet isolated. ### Edited illustrations of the symptom The following are **AI-edited, de-branded illustrations**, derived from supplied images. The original mascot has been replaced with a neutral gray circle. They illustrate the visual difference only: **they are not unmodified diagnostic screenshots, captured frames of a minimal reproducer, or evidence of a particular root cause**. The two source backgrounds/scales differ. | Opaque black rectangle around the subject (symptom illustration) | Background visible around the subject (normal-transparency illustration) | | --- | --- | | | | ### Reproduction **No reliable natural reproducer or public minimal reproduction repository yet.** The observed production scenario is: 1. Open a transparent desktop-pet window with transparent page styling and keep it alive. 2. Use the application normally for an extended period. 3. At an unknown point, the transparent area becomes an opaque black rectangle while the character remains visible. The available logs contain display changes and screen-capture device re-enumeration; the detailed timeline is below. They do not establish when the first black frame appeared. Local exploratory tests have not produced sustained black backgrounds after changing another monitor's resolution, sending the graphics-reset shortcut, monitor power cycling, or repeatedly terminating/restarting the WebView2 GPU process. These tests have limitations: the resolution test excluded the monitor hosting the pet, sampling was not continuous, and build identity was not fully recorded. They do not exclude these failure classes. Next planned tests are real unplug/replug of the monitor hosting the pet, changes to that monitor's resolution/refresh rate, and extend/single-display transitions while preserving the same pet HWND. **These are proposed experiments, not verified reproduction steps.** ### Separate controlled experiment: fault injection only On the old installed app, deliberately calling `DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow` with `fEnable = FALSE` for the pet HWND produces visually similar black transparent areas while the character remains visible. Sending only an artificial `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED` does not restore the old build. Reapplying the creation-time empty-region blur-behind parameters, followed by `SetWindowPos(SWP_FRAMECHANGED)` and `InvalidateRect`, restores transparency on the same HWND. This directly alters native transparency state. It is **not a natural reproducer and does not prove that Windows performed the same state change in production**. The recovery experiment changes several things together, so it does not isolate which operation is necessary. ### Expected behavior Transparent regions should remain correctly composed throughout supported display configuration changes. If native transparency/composition state requires reinitialization, the windowing/webview integration should recover it without requiring the application to destroy and recreate the window. ### Full `tauri info` output ```text Full tauri info output from the affected machine is unavailable. The following is a manually collected summary, NOT generated tauri info output. Affected application release: 2.88.1.610 (application version, not Tauri version) Affected OS: Windows 11, build 26200 Affected WebView2 Runtime version: not captured Affected GPU/driver: not captured Cargo.lock package versions from the investigated source tree: tauri 2.3.1 tauri-runtime 2.4.0 tauri-runtime-wry 2.4.1 tao 0.32.8 wry 0.50.3 IMPORTANT: These are maintained forks, not an unmodified crates.io dependency set. The installed affected package's exact source-commit mapping has not been established. Reproduction on the latest unmodified upstream release has not been established either. These version numbers describe the investigated source tree; they are not proof of an upstream regression. ``` ### Stack trace ```text ``` ### Additional context ### Important application-specific native behavior: SetWindowRgn and non-client painting An important detail missing from the initial report: **our application also calls `SetWindowRgn` and overrides non-client painting for windows with an active custom region.** Please consider this when assessing whether the problem is in upstream Tauri/tao/wry or in our integration. We have not isolated a causal link or established a clean A/B result with these customizations disabled. For the native hit region, the implementation unions rectangles into an HRGN and calls `SetWindowRgn(hwnd, Some(region), true)`. The region is used so points outside the interactive shape can reach underlying windows. This clips **drawing as well as hit testing**; the supplied region must include all visible content. The reason for the non-client workaround is a separate caption artifact we observed after applying a window region: our understanding is that the default non-client drawing path can draw a classic caption based on the `WS_CAPTION`/`WS_SYSMENU` styles retained by tao, while tao handles `WM_NCCALCSIZE` to treat the full window as client area. The unwanted caption then appears over the page. We suppress non-client painting for region-managed windows rather than repeatedly clearing styles that tao may restore. This is our application workaround rationale, not a confirmed explanation of the black-background failure. The dispatch routes only these four messages to the helper: - `WM_NCPAINT` - `WM_NCACTIVATE` - `WM_NCUAHDRAWCAPTION` (`0x00AE`) - `WM_NCUAHDRAWFRAME` (`0x00AF`) Our helper is: ```rust unsafe fn handle_nc_paint( state: &WindowState, hwnd: HWND, msg: u32, wparam: WPARAM, ) -> Option { if !crate::window_hit_region::region_active() || !crate::window_hit_region::has_region(state.window.label()) { return None; } if msg == WM_NCACTIVATE { return Some(call_origin_window_proc(hwnd, msg, wparam, LPARAM(-1))); } Some(LRESULT(0)) } ``` `None` lets normal processing continue; `Some` returns directly from our window procedure. The `WM_NCACTIVATE` branch still forwards to the original window procedure (tao) to retain activation/focus handling, but passes `lParam = -1` to suppress non-client repaint. For the other three routed messages, the helper returns zero without calling the original procedure when the region is active. **This is not a stock-Tauri-only window configuration.** The existing fork/affected-binary mapping limitations still apply. We would like to determine whether these region/non-client customizations can interfere with transparent-window composition before treating DWM re-registration as an upstream fix. ### Key log observations from the affected session Selected timestamps and message text, with application/process metadata omitted (not a complete raw log): ```text 17:48:53.665 screen_capture_win.c:251 display changed 17:48:55.020 screen_capture_win.c:251 display changed 17:48:55.940 xc_device_manager.c:147 'screen-capture' enum start 17:48:56.501 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://device_changed 17:48:56.527 looper_monitor.cc:96 dtmp.main Overdue 2808 ms. 17:48:56.538 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://display_changed 18:09:27.320 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://device_changed 18:09:27.322 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://device_changed ``` - The first capture-side display event is almost three seconds earlier than the pet's bridged event. The bridge logs after asynchronous dispatch to the main thread; its timestamp is not the native message-arrival time. Adjacent bridge lines cannot establish exact native-message order. - The later 18:09 device-change burst has no corresponding display-change entry. Device events do not identify the changed device or prove a graphics/composition failure. - Main/tips window DPI callbacks after the first burst report scale 1.000. Without the prior value, this does not establish that DPI changed. Raw display-message parameters, adapter identity, and monitor topology were not captured. - The application-main-process PID is unchanged across the captured session. Pet dragging and menu actions are still logged near the report, so this is not a whole-application crash. - Periodic CPU samples list the pet WebView and WebView2 GPU process by name, but omit their PIDs/creation times. They cannot exclude an intervening GPU-process restart or a composition failure in a live process. - No logged `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED`, webview-crash callback, or explicit background-color-change message was found. This is not proof that all rendering/composition state stayed healthy; the older path did not provide complete native-message/failure-kind instrumentation. - Logs cover approximately 17:01–18:52, with user feedback at 18:52. We do not know the first black frame, so cannot claim it failed at 17:48 or remained black for that whole interval. ### Investigation and experimental mitigation In the investigated source, tao enables transparency with `DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow` and an empty region during window creation; wry separately configures the WebView2 default-background alpha. We treat native-window transparency and WebView background/composition as distinct layers. We prototyped a native-window mitigation that observes `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` and `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED`, forwards normal processing first, then schedules the following on the window thread: 1. Reapply `DWM_BB_ENABLE | DWM_BB_BLURREGION`, `fEnable = TRUE`, and an empty region from `CreateRectRgn(0, 0, -1, -1)`. 2. Request `SetWindowPos` with `SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER`. 3. Request repaint with `InvalidateRect`. The prototype coalesces notifications and currently uses a 100 ms delay. It restores the injected failure when an artificial notification is sent, but **its effectiveness and timing against the natural production failure are unverified**. We recognize that Windows 8+ keeps DWM composition enabled and does not send `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED` merely because the video mode changes. Artificial notification testing does not validate Windows 11 event/recovery coverage: [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dwm/wm-dwmcompositionchanged). ### Questions for maintainers 1. Does this appear to belong to the same failure class as #15947, or should the recovery investigation be tracked in tao/wry instead? 2. Is reapplying empty-region blur-behind after `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` a supported recovery strategy? What ordering/events are appropriate on Windows 11, where relying on `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED` is insufficient? 3. What diagnostics best distinguish native transparency-state failure from WebView2 background/DirectComposition or graphics-device recovery failure? We plan raw window-message parameters, display topology/adapter identity, WebView2 `ProcessFailed` kind/reason, process lifetimes, and timestamped before/after video. 4. Would the `no_redirection_bitmap` path discussed in #15410 be appropriate to evaluate for this window type, and what compatibility constraints should we consider? 5. Could `SetWindowRgn` together with the non-client suppression above interfere with transparent-window composition or recovery? What controlled A/B test or alternative approach would you recommend to isolate our integration from upstream behavior? We would particularly appreciate suggestions for a **real system-level trigger** or an upstream minimal test case that reproduces this failure class without directly disabling blur-behind or fabricating composition notifications.

The original mascot has been replaced with a neutral gray circle. They illustrate the visual difference only: **they are not unmodified diagnostic screenshots, captured frames of a minimal reproducer, or evidence of a particular root cause**. The two source backgrounds/scales differ. | Opaque black rectangle around the subject (symptom illustration) | Background visible around the subject (normal-transparency illustration) | | --- | --- | | | | ### Reproduction **No reliable natural reproducer or public minimal reproduction repository yet.** The observed production scenario is: 1. Open a transparent desktop-pet window with transparent page styling and keep it alive. 2. Use the application normally for an extended period. 3. At an unknown point, the transparent area becomes an opaque black rectangle while the character remains visible. The available logs contain display changes and screen-capture device re-enumeration; the detailed timeline is below. They do not establish when the first black frame appeared. Local exploratory tests have not produced sustained black backgrounds after changing another monitor's resolution, sending the graphics-reset shortcut, monitor power cycling, or repeatedly terminating/restarting the WebView2 GPU process. These tests have limitations: the resolution test excluded the monitor hosting the pet, sampling was not continuous, and build identity was not fully recorded. They do not exclude these failure classes. Next planned tests are real unplug/replug of the monitor hosting the pet, changes to that monitor's resolution/refresh rate, and extend/single-display transitions while preserving the same pet HWND. **These are proposed experiments, not verified reproduction steps.** ### Separate controlled experiment: fault injection only On the old installed app, deliberately calling `DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow` with `fEnable = FALSE` for the pet HWND produces visually similar black transparent areas while the character remains visible. Sending only an artificial `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED` does not restore the old build. Reapplying the creation-time empty-region blur-behind parameters, followed by `SetWindowPos(SWP_FRAMECHANGED)` and `InvalidateRect`, restores transparency on the same HWND. This directly alters native transparency state. It is **not a natural reproducer and does not prove that Windows performed the same state change in production**. The recovery experiment changes several things together, so it does not isolate which operation is necessary. ### Expected behavior Transparent regions should remain correctly composed throughout supported display configuration changes. If native transparency/composition state requires reinitialization, the windowing/webview integration should recover it without requiring the application to destroy and recreate the window. ### Full `tauri info` output ```text Full tauri info output from the affected machine is unavailable. The following is a manually collected summary, NOT generated tauri info output. Affected application release: 2.88.1.610 (application version, not Tauri version) Affected OS: Windows 11, build 26200 Affected WebView2 Runtime version: not captured Affected GPU/driver: not captured Cargo.lock package versions from the investigated source tree: tauri 2.3.1 tauri-runtime 2.4.0 tauri-runtime-wry 2.4.1 tao 0.32.8 wry 0.50.3 IMPORTANT: These are maintained forks, not an unmodified crates.io dependency set. The installed affected package's exact source-commit mapping has not been established. Reproduction on the latest unmodified upstream release has not been established either. These version numbers describe the investigated source tree; they are not proof of an upstream regression. ``` ### Stack trace ```text ``` ### Additional context ### Important application-specific native behavior: SetWindowRgn and non-client painting An important detail missing from the initial report: **our application also calls `SetWindowRgn` and overrides non-client painting for windows with an active custom region.** Please consider this when assessing whether the problem is in upstream Tauri/tao/wry or in our integration. We have not isolated a causal link or established a clean A/B result with these customizations disabled. For the native hit region, the implementation unions rectangles into an HRGN and calls `SetWindowRgn(hwnd, Some(region), true)`. The region is used so points outside the interactive shape can reach underlying windows. This clips **drawing as well as hit testing**; the supplied region must include all visible content. The reason for the non-client workaround is a separate caption artifact we observed after applying a window region: our understanding is that the default non-client drawing path can draw a classic caption based on the `WS_CAPTION`/`WS_SYSMENU` styles retained by tao, while tao handles `WM_NCCALCSIZE` to treat the full window as client area. The unwanted caption then appears over the page. We suppress non-client painting for region-managed windows rather than repeatedly clearing styles that tao may restore. This is our application workaround rationale, not a confirmed explanation of the black-background failure. The dispatch routes only these four messages to the helper: - `WM_NCPAINT` - `WM_NCACTIVATE` - `WM_NCUAHDRAWCAPTION` (`0x00AE`) - `WM_NCUAHDRAWFRAME` (`0x00AF`) Our helper is: ```rust unsafe fn handle_nc_paint( state: &WindowState, hwnd: HWND, msg: u32, wparam: WPARAM, ) -> Option { if !crate::window_hit_region::region_active() || !crate::window_hit_region::has_region(state.window.label()) { return None; } if msg == WM_NCACTIVATE { return Some(call_origin_window_proc(hwnd, msg, wparam, LPARAM(-1))); } Some(LRESULT(0)) } ``` `None` lets normal processing continue; `Some` returns directly from our window procedure. The `WM_NCACTIVATE` branch still forwards to the original window procedure (tao) to retain activation/focus handling, but passes `lParam = -1` to suppress non-client repaint. For the other three routed messages, the helper returns zero without calling the original procedure when the region is active. **This is not a stock-Tauri-only window configuration.** The existing fork/affected-binary mapping limitations still apply. We would like to determine whether these region/non-client customizations can interfere with transparent-window composition before treating DWM re-registration as an upstream fix. ### Key log observations from the affected session Selected timestamps and message text, with application/process metadata omitted (not a complete raw log): ```text 17:48:53.665 screen_capture_win.c:251 display changed 17:48:55.020 screen_capture_win.c:251 display changed 17:48:55.940 xc_device_manager.c:147 'screen-capture' enum start 17:48:56.501 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://device_changed 17:48:56.527 looper_monitor.cc:96 dtmp.main Overdue 2808 ms. 17:48:56.538 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://display_changed 18:09:27.320 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://device_changed 18:09:27.322 emit_util.rs:64 emit_to_webview_event label:pet event:bridge_api://device_changed ``` - The first capture-side display event is almost three seconds earlier than the pet's bridged event. The bridge logs after asynchronous dispatch to the main thread; its timestamp is not the native message-arrival time. Adjacent bridge lines cannot establish exact native-message order. - The later 18:09 device-change burst has no corresponding display-change entry. Device events do not identify the changed device or prove a graphics/composition failure. - Main/tips window DPI callbacks after the first burst report scale 1.000. Without the prior value, this does not establish that DPI changed. Raw display-message parameters, adapter identity, and monitor topology were not captured. - The application-main-process PID is unchanged across the captured session. Pet dragging and menu actions are still logged near the report, so this is not a whole-application crash. - Periodic CPU samples list the pet WebView and WebView2 GPU process by name, but omit their PIDs/creation times. They cannot exclude an intervening GPU-process restart or a composition failure in a live process. - No logged `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED`, webview-crash callback, or explicit background-color-change message was found. This is not proof that all rendering/composition state stayed healthy; the older path did not provide complete native-message/failure-kind instrumentation. - Logs cover approximately 17:01–18:52, with user feedback at 18:52. We do not know the first black frame, so cannot claim it failed at 17:48 or remained black for that whole interval. ### Investigation and experimental mitigation In the investigated source, tao enables transparency with `DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow` and an empty region during window creation; wry separately configures the WebView2 default-background alpha. We treat native-window transparency and WebView background/composition as distinct layers. We prototyped a native-window mitigation that observes `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` and `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED`, forwards normal processing first, then schedules the following on the window thread: 1. Reapply `DWM_BB_ENABLE | DWM_BB_BLURREGION`, `fEnable = TRUE`, and an empty region from `CreateRectRgn(0, 0, -1, -1)`. 2. Request `SetWindowPos` with `SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER`. 3. Request repaint with `InvalidateRect`. The prototype coalesces notifications and currently uses a 100 ms delay. It restores the injected failure when an artificial notification is sent, but **its effectiveness and timing against the natural production failure are unverified**. We recognize that Windows 8+ keeps DWM composition enabled and does not send `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED` merely because the video mode changes. Artificial notification testing does not validate Windows 11 event/recovery coverage: [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dwm/wm-dwmcompositionchanged). ### Questions for maintainers 1. Does this appear to belong to the same failure class as #15947, or should the recovery investigation be tracked in tao/wry instead? 2. Is reapplying empty-region blur-behind after `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` a supported recovery strategy? What ordering/events are appropriate on Windows 11, where relying on `WM_DWMCOMPOSITIONCHANGED` is insufficient? 3. What diagnostics best distinguish native transparency-state failure from WebView2 background/DirectComposition or graphics-device recovery failure? We plan raw window-message parameters, display topology/adapter identity, WebView2 `ProcessFailed` kind/reason, process lifetimes, and timestamped before/after video. 4. Would the `no_redirection_bitmap` path discussed in #15410 be appropriate to evaluate for this window type, and what compatibility constraints should we consider? 5. Could `SetWindowRgn` together with the non-client suppression above interfere with transparent-window composition or recovery? What controlled A/B test or alternative approach would you recommend to isolate our integration from upstream behavior? We would particularly appreciate suggestions for a **real system-level trigger** or an upstream minimal test case that reproduces this failure class without directly disabling blur-behind or fabricating composition notifications.", "language": "Rust", "state": "open", "assignees": [], "locked": false, "verified_at": "2026-10-22T17:43:36.149Z", "expires_at": "2026-10-23T17:43:36.149000+00:00", "timeline_complete": true, "bucket": "historical_signal_only"}

### Describe the bug

When a window loses focus it does not regain keyboard input after refocus unless clicked on. 

### Reproduction

1. Run examples/cef 
2. Navigate focus away depending on OS and Desktop
3. Return focus to cef window
4. Press f12 (Nothing happens)
5. click on window and then press f12 (it works)

Keyboard input returns to the page when it is refocused,
